wiki-iran.standing: A daily count of how many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so each spike points to an event rather than to the country itself.
wiki-iran.recent: The peak followed Trump's threat to 'annihilate' Iran in his UN speech. Talks in New York then turned to terms for reopening Hormuz, and Tehran now says the strait stays shut until 7 conditions are met while its foreign ministry debates quitting the nuclear treaty. Iran denies any link to the suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford.

brent.standing: Crude from the North Sea, and the reference against which about two-thirds of internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel, jet fuel and freight costs follow it, so it reaches inflation in every importing country.
brent.recent: A war with Iran shut the Strait of Hormuz, the passage for roughly a fifth of the world's oil; Aramco counts almost 3 billion barrels of supply lost. The retreat from the peak followed New York talks on reopening terms, a G7 stock release and Middle East exports recovering past pre-war levels, though tankers are still being struck.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate, the light, low-sulphur crude delivered by pipeline to Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' decisions to pump.
wti.recent: An Iranian blockade on Hormuz cut Gulf supply and drove the climb; Kuwait still pumps about 75% of its prewar oil. The retreat from the peak came as non-Iranian crude flows through the strait returned to the pre-war 13.5 million barrels a day and the International Energy Agency committed 100 million barrels of oil and fuel from reserves.

natgas-hh.standing: The price of natural gas delivered at Henry Hub, a pipeline junction in Louisiana, and the benchmark for US gas. It feeds American heating and power bills, and US LNG export contracts are priced off it.
natgas-hh.recent: The gas news of these weeks was shortage abroad. The war on Iran restricted traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which Qatar's LNG must cross, and Pakistan sought 22 winter cargoes and may get 12. None of it accounts for the US price itself, which is set by domestic supply and weather.

wheat.standing: The world price of a tonne of wheat, the most widely traded food grain. Importing states from North Africa to South Asia buy against it, so it reaches the cost of bread and the size of government subsidy bills.
wheat.recent: The fortnight's news shows what dearer wheat does rather than what lifted it. A National Assembly committee in Pakistan wants a Rs5,000 per 40kg support price, Egypt delayed a second bread price request in months, and India closed its weakest monsoon since 2015 under a strong El Niño.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, 5% broken, the reference grade for the world's most widely eaten staple. Only a small share of the crop crosses borders, so one exporter's ban or bad harvest moves it fast.
rice.recent: India's monsoon ended 12.6% below the long-term average, the weakest since 2015, while floods killed at least 62 people in Uttar Pradesh and Bangkok had its worst floods in 15 years. All of that falls on rice-growing land, but this monthly series ends before any of it, and none of it accounts for the earlier fall.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in nearly every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, most of all in China, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and Congo.
copper.recent: China made guaranteed copper supply a condition of approving the Anglo Teck merger, three sources say, and India approved ₹1.86 lakh crore for transmission lines, which are built from the metal. Both are buyers moving to lock in supply, but neither accounts for the price.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other countries' debt are priced off it, so a move here reaches borrowers far outside America.
us-10y.recent: Lenders sold government debt everywhere, not only in Washington: average global yields neared 4%, the highest since 2007, and Japan's 10-year hit 3.11%. The US already pays about $1 trillion a year in interest, and Trump tied $5,000 checks, estimated above $1 trillion, to the midterms.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the climb, and most of it ran the other way. Fed officials questioned JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley over private credit, the US pays about $1 trillion a year in interest as bond yields rise, and Brent crude stayed above $100 a barrel even after the G7 pledged a release of stocks.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in the United States, weighted by market value. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it works as a gauge of what investors pay for big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: The run-up brought favourable news for the index's heaviest members: Nvidia authorized a record $150 billion share buyback, Meta launched a paid AI platform for businesses, and a judge dismissed the Chegg and Penske antitrust suits against Google. Trump and top tech firms also signed an accord to self-police AI development.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price American drivers pay at the pump for a gallon of regular gasoline, as surveyed by the Energy Information Administration. It follows crude oil and refining costs, and few prices weigh more on US voters.
us-gas-retail.recent: Fuel has climbed since the Iran war began, and diesel has led it: it set a record, and Trump told Europe to release its diesel reserves or lose US supply. With midterms close, a third of states cut fuel taxes, and the International Energy Agency agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of gas at the Title Transfer Facility, a Dutch virtual trading hub, and the benchmark for European gas contracts. Power prices and heating bills across the continent follow it, and it sets what Europe bids for LNG.
natgas-ttf.recent: Qatar's LNG leaves through the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran says is shut, and unlike Saudi crude it has no pipeline around it, so the US-Iran war took cargoes that European and Asian buyers compete for off the market. Tankers loaded at Ras Laffan are now reappearing outside the strait, and September shipments were the highest since the war began.

vix.standing: A measure of how much movement options traders are pricing into the S&P 500 over the next 30 days, calculated by the CBOE. It rises when investors pay up for protection against falling shares, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: The stress of late September sat in the bond market rather than in shares: Treasury volatility jumped from 80 to 104 in 2 days while stocks stayed calm. Nothing else in the fortnight's news accounts for the equity side.

fx-pkr.standing: How many Pakistani rupees buy one US dollar. Pakistan imports most of its fuel and owes much of its foreign debt in dollars, so the rate feeds straight into pump prices, inflation and the cost of servicing that debt.
fx-pkr.recent: The fortnight's news from Islamabad was domestic: a petrol price rise, a fuel subsidy for motorcycle riders under review, a winter gas plan after Pakistan sought 22 cargoes and may get 12, and Imran Khan's party marching on the capital after talks failed. None of it accounts for the rupee's rate.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, priced in naira per US dollar. Oil exports earn most of the country's dollars, so the rate follows crude and central-bank policy, and it sets what Nigerians pay for imported fuel, food and medicine.
fx-ngn.recent: Auditors found ₦1.63 trillion unaccounted for at Nigeria's central bank, the state oil company lost 77.6% of its fuel-products revenue, and the World Bank's private-sector arm committed $50 million to guarantor InfraCredit. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-egp.standing: Egypt's currency, quoted as pounds per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker pound. Egypt is among the world's largest wheat importers and carries heavy dollar debt, so each fall reaches bread prices and the state budget.
fx-egp.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news from Cairo accounts for the pound's weakening. The stories were about the security state rather than the economy: all six journalists of the fact-checking outlet Matsda2sh were arrested within two days, and an Italian court convicted three Egyptian agents over the kidnap of Giulio Regeni.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira one US dollar buys. Turkey imports nearly all its oil and gas and its companies borrow heavily in dollars, so a weaker lira feeds straight into inflation and debt costs.
fx-try.recent: Turkey's recent weeks were about security rather than money: it pledged troops to Saudi Arabia alongside Pakistan, agreed to pass its Bashiqa base to Iraqi control, and a cargo ship sank off Romania in the Black Sea. None of it accounts for the lira's slow slide.

fx-bdt.standing: How many Bangladeshi taka buy one US dollar. Bangladesh pays for its fuel, cotton and machinery in dollars and earns them from garment exports and workers' remittances, so the rate sets the cost of imports for 170 million people.

fx-idr.standing: Indonesia's currency, quoted as rupiah per US dollar, so a rising line is a weaker rupiah. Indonesia imports fuel and borrows in dollars, so a slide raises costs at home and often draws the central bank in.
fx-idr.recent: Indonesia has a new finance minister, who faces a test of delivery. Nothing else reported in these weeks bears on the currency, and the appointment alone does not account for the rupiah's weakening.

fx-lbp.standing: How many Lebanese pounds buy one US dollar. The currency lost nearly all its value in the banking collapse that began in 2019, and the central bank now holds it at a managed rate in an economy that runs largely on dollars.
fx-lbp.recent: The news about Lebanon in these weeks was about security, not money: Israeli minister Smotrich called for annexing parts of the country, and Israel pressed for a US-led force to disarm Hezbollah. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-cny.standing: China's currency, quoted as yuan per US dollar. The central bank sets a daily midpoint and allows trading only in a narrow band around it, so the rate is a policy signal as much as a market price, and it sets the cost of Chinese exports.
fx-cny.recent: Xi Jinping's three-day trip to Washington fell inside the window, and his summit with Trump wrapped with little changed in the trade war between the two. With no deal struck and no new measure announced, a managed currency was given nothing to reprice.

fx-inr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Indian rupees, so a rising line is a weaker rupee. India buys most of its oil abroad in dollars, so the rate carries crude costs into fuel and food prices, and the central bank intervenes to steady it.
fx-inr.recent: India imports most of its oil, so the war premium on Brent crude raised its dollar bill just as US bond yields climbed, and the Sensex fell for seven straight weeks. The Reserve Bank of India answered with its first rate hike since 2023, passed 6-0, on the day a tanker was struck in Hormuz.

fx-brl.standing: The number of Brazilian reais one US dollar buys, so a falling line is a stronger real. It moves on the prices of the soy, iron ore and oil Brazil exports, and on how far investors trust Brasília's public finances.
fx-brl.recent: The real was weakest on the day Brazil's final debate was cancelled two days before the vote, with the Banco Master fraud scandal, which cost the deposit insurer $7.7bn, hanging over the presidential race. It firmed once the first round was counted: Flávio Bolsonaro beat Lula 47% to 45.1%, and the election goes to a runoff.

fx-mxn.standing: How many Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Mexico sells most of its exports to the United States, and the rate moves on US trade policy and sets the value of remittances migrants send home.
fx-mxn.recent: Sheinbaum asked Washington for evidence of the cross-border shooting the US used to justify sending 500 troops to the frontier, days after 14 Latin American nations declared cartels foreign terrorist organizations and Hurricane Polo twice made landfall on the Pacific coast. None of it is a reported cause of the peso's move.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys, the exchange rate between the world's two most used currencies. It moves on the gap between European Central Bank and Federal Reserve interest rates, and on the price of the energy Europe imports.
fx-eur.recent: An energy shock from the Middle East war is running through the euro area: inflation jumped in September, and the European Central Bank has already been raising its rate. Business activity still grew at its fastest pace in nearly three and a half years, while the US pressed Europe to release emergency diesel stocks.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen buy one US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker yen. Japan's low interest rates make it the currency the world borrows cheaply in, and its swings move import costs at home and funding costs abroad.
fx-jpy.recent: Japan's 10-year yield hit 3.11%, near a 30-year high, in a global bond sell-off, and three sources say the Bank of Japan may declare underlying inflation has reached its 2% target, clearing the way for rate rises. Both would normally pull money home and lift the yen; neither accounts for its slide against the dollar.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns most of its hard currency from oil and gas exports, so the rate moves with energy prices, sanctions and the central bank's capital controls, and import prices follow it.
fx-rub.recent: The fortnight pulled two ways. Peskov confirmed energy talks with US negotiators and Trump invited Putin to the Miami G20; against that, Washington may decide by 18 October on secondary sanctions, and Ukraine says it has put more than 51% of Russia's oil refining capacity out of action. Nothing here accounts for the rate itself.

fx-zar.standing: What one US dollar costs in South African rand, the most heavily traded currency in Africa. It moves with gold and platinum prices and with appetite for emerging-market risk, and sets what South Africans pay for imported fuel.
fx-zar.recent: The fortnight's news from South Africa was about violence and diplomacy rather than money: gunmen killed 27 people in two Gauteng townships, Pretoria was hit with punitive US travel bans, and Gold Fields had an A$39bn bid for Northern Star rejected. None of it accounts for the rand's move.

btc.standing: The oldest and largest cryptocurrency, with supply capped at 21 million coins and no issuer behind it. It trades around the clock as a gauge of appetite for risk, and the rest of the crypto market moves with it.
btc.recent: The rally broke when traders priced in 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027, which pulls money away from assets that pay no yield. A $350 million theft from the exchange Bitget and the death of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act in the US Senate followed within days. The US then approved its first 3x leveraged crypto funds.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, paid as the fee for every transaction and program run on it. Most stablecoins and decentralised finance settle there, so its price tracks how much that economy is used.
eth.recent: Nothing in the news explains the late-September peak. After it, hackers took $350 million from Bitget and drained Duelbits, and the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act died in the US Senate. Since then the US approved its first 3x leveraged crypto funds, and developers patched the Glamsterdam upgrade before its Sepolia test.

paxg.standing: The price of a troy ounce of gold, read here from PAX Gold, a token backed by bars held in London vaults. Gold pays no interest, so it moves against bond yields and the dollar, and central banks hold it as a reserve.
paxg.recent: Gold pays no interest, so it lost ground as Treasury yields surged and the US dollar strengthened. Rising oil prices sat alongside both: fuel costs have climbed since the Iran war began, and the International Energy Agency agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel from reserves.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: The daily count of people opening Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence. It rises when the technology breaks out of the trade press and a general audience goes looking for the basics.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: OpenAI warned more than 100 organisations that its models may have entered their systems, and its safety-report lead David Robinson quit days later. In Washington, Trump named intelligence director Jay Clayton to lead a new task force, and six executives signed a one-page accord with no legal force.

wiki-russia.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It counts readers, not events: a jump marks a day when the war, the Kremlin or a crisis inside the country sent people to look the country up.
wiki-russia.recent: A 28-year-old technician at the Irkutsk anti-plague institute died and dozens were quarantined; authorities name pneumonia and deny imposing anti-plague measures. Ukraine sent 650 drones at Moscow by the mayor's count, killing two, as the Kremlin confirmed energy talks with US negotiators.

wiki-china.standing: The number of people who open Wikipedia's article on China each day. It is a rough gauge of when the world's second-largest economy has pushed into public curiosity, and it jumps on summits, crises and disasters.
wiki-china.recent: Xi Jinping spent three days in Washington with Trump, a visit that wrapped with little changed beyond $30bn in tariff cuts led by farm goods and holiday decorations. The peak came days later, as Trump denied asking Xi about potential US arms sales, after a US envoy said Beijing had assured Washington it isn't aiding Iran.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman that links the Persian Gulf to the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, so a closure reaches fuel prices everywhere.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Iran holds the strait shut until 7 conditions are met, after Trump rejected its proposal to reopen it and the talks moved through Qatari mediators. Ships cross anyway: Iraq sent 2 million barrels on a state tanker and Qatari LNG cargoes cleared, while projectiles hit tankers, one injuring 12 crew on the On Peace.

wiki-india.standing: The number of people who open Wikipedia's article on India each day. It is the world's most populous country, and the count jumps when an election, a disaster or a border clash sends outsiders looking for the basics.
wiki-india.recent: The fortnight's story is a fight over the voter rolls: Congress says 130 million names were deleted, a sitting Supreme Court judge called the deletions arbitrary, and police in New Delhi detained 260 people including Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi. The central bank raised rates for the first time since 2023. None of it explains the September peak.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran says the strait stays shut until 7 conditions are met, and the US answered its 7-day plan through Qatar. Some ships cross anyway: more Qatari LNG tankers cleared over the weekend, and Kuwait pumps about 75% of prewar oil. Then a projectile hit the tanker On Peace off the Omani port of Limah, injuring 12 crew.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: The war for the strait's Yemeni shore opened this week. Saudi-backed Yemeni forces say they retook Mokha and secured Dhubab, cutting Houthi roads to Bab el-Mandeb, and blasts erupted beside a tanker off Mokha. Houthis answered by hitting 2 Saudi airports, and Pakistan and Turkey pledged troops to Saudi Arabia.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: The fighting is at the far end of the Red Sea: the Yemeni army says it secured Dhubab, beside Bab al-Mandab, and retook Mocha, while Saudi Arabia plans an offensive against the Houthis and two Saudi airports were targeted. None of it accounts for the canal's traffic.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The traffic that feeds this strait from the west recovered: Middle East crude exports peaked at 22.5 million barrels daily on Kpler data, more Qatari LNG tankers cleared Hormuz, and Iraq sent 2 million barrels through on a state tanker. Strikes on tankers in Hormuz and off Mokha continued, and nothing reported explains the July swings.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: The fortnight around the strait was political rather than maritime: Xi's visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, Taipei received the first 2 of 66 ordered F-16V fighters, and the Philippines says it forced a Chinese survey ship from Batanes. None of it reached the shipping lanes or accounts for the traffic.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Ships on the lanes that feed the strait came under attack. A cargo ship sank off Romania with 2 crew dead, in what Ukraine says was a Russian drone strike; drones then sank the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, and a crude tanker burned off Sochi. That coast is the route grain and oil take to Istanbul.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The fortnight's news on both shores was political rather than maritime: Morocco named its first female prime minister, Sánchez called a snap election in Spain, and thousands of migrants were stranded in Ceuta. None of it accounts for the traffic through the strait.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Blasts beside a tanker off Mokha, near Bab el-Mandeb, kept the Red Sea approach dangerous in early October, and that danger is why ships take this detour. The strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, including the projectile that hit On Peace, bear on Gulf oil rather than this route, and nothing reported accounts for the swings here.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Nothing reported in the past fortnight accounts for the strait itself. The attacks on shipping were out in the open Black Sea: drones sank the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan off Bulgaria, leaving its crew missing, a cargo ship went down off Romania with 2 crew dead, and a crude tanker burned off Sochi.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index, which tracks every main-market company on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh. It is the Arab world's largest market by value and Aramco dominates it. It trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week.
mkt:tadawul.recent: In the window, the main news touching Saudi Arabia was the Houthi advance: they seized a key port and took control of Yemen's Red Sea coast, a vital shipping route. None of it was reported in terms of Saudi-listed companies, and none of it accounts for the index's move.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so its level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Turkey's news in these weeks was about security rather than its companies: it agreed to pass its Bashiqa base to Iraqi control, pledged troops to Saudi Arabia alongside Pakistan as Houthi drones reached Riyadh, and a cargo ship sank in the Black Sea off Romania. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Dubai Financial Market General Index tracks the shares listed on Dubai's stock exchange, the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking. It trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The fortnight brought the war to Dubai's doorstep. Missiles fell on Gulf cities, the Hormuz closure pushed Emirati trade overland through Oman, the UAE suspended trade with Iran in August, and Algeria cut ties. None of it falls on the dates of the index's high or low, so none of it explains the price.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index tracks the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national stock exchange. The exchange is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Malaysia's fortnight held the deportation of 1,476 Myanmar detainees on navy ships from Lumut, the death of former first lady Siti Hasmah at 100, and the Mihas 2026 halal trade showcase in Kuala Lumpur. None of it accounts for the index.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, weighted by size. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and banks and commodity producers carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: Nothing published in the past fortnight accounts for the index's path. The news from Indonesia was about a new finance minister facing a test of delivery, and about MSCI rating 80% of Chinese mining firms as laggards on sustainability, neither of which is tied to a move in Jakarta's shares.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. It is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Japan's 10-year yield hit 3.11%, near a 30-year high, in a global bond sell-off, and three sources say the Bank of Japan may declare its 2% inflation goal reached. Factory activity growth slowed in September. Higher borrowing costs and slower factories weigh on shares, so none of this accounts for the index's climb.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Mainland Chinese firms meet foreign capital here, making it the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: Xi's three-day visit to Washington ended with little changed between the two governments. Days later Macron and Merz asked Brussels for the power to cut China off from the EU market, with Berlin no longer acting as the brake on such steps. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:sse.standing: Every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board, weighted by size. The market is largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: Xi's three-day visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, and the tariff cuts China and the US announced afterwards, $30bn led by farm goods and holiday decorations, were narrow. Paris and Berlin have since asked for the power to cut off EU market access. None of it accounts for the index's move.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, which makes it a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The fortnight's news from Seoul was diplomatic rather than financial: landmines that wounded 3 South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone, a row with Ukraine over North Korean prisoners, and a disputed $54bn Alaska gas pledge. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 large, heavily traded companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and the index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The Reserve Bank of India raised its repo rate to 5.5%, its first hike since 2023, on a 6-0 vote as inflation climbs. India imports most of its oil, so rising Brent crude arrives as fuel and food prices. A projectile hit the tanker On Peace in the Strait of Hormuz, the passage for roughly a fifth of the world's oil.

mkt:sgx.standing: The Straits Times Index tracks the 30 largest companies listed on the Singapore Exchange, Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three local banks carry much of its weight, alongside regional property groups.
mkt:sgx.recent: Nothing filed from Singapore in the window concerned its listed banks or property firms. The stories datelined there were about Middle East crude exports and a slide in gold as Treasury yields surged, and neither accounts for the index.

mkt:twse.standing: Every common stock listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in Taipei, weighted by market value. TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes it the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fortnight's news about Taiwan was diplomatic and military, not commercial: Xi pressed Trump in Washington to oppose independence, Trump denied asking Xi about US arms sales, and the first 2 of 66 ordered F-16V fighters landed in Taipei. None of it accounts for the index.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It moves with tourism flows and with regional energy prices.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSE Composite Index: 30 of the largest, most traded companies on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila. It is a small market driven by the domestic economy, and money sent home by Filipinos working abroad moves the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The fortnight's Philippine news was a ferry fire off Coron, a school shooting in Banga, Bangsamoro's first parliamentary election and an anti-graft court's arrest warrant for Romualdez over flood-control kickbacks. None of it touches listed earnings or remittance flows, and none of it explains the index's slide.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Miners and the big banks dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Annual inflation hit 4.0% in August, up from 3.5%, despite a run of rate hikes, leaving borrowing costs no room to fall. The miners carry their own exposure: China buys three-fifths of Australia's iron ore exports. Trump weighing a diesel export ban added a fuel threat for a country that imports it.

mkt:jse.standing: The FTSE/JSE All Share Index covers nearly all the market value listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in South Africa. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the continent's only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The fortnight's news from South Africa was mass shootings in Gauteng and Durban, a US visa dispute with Pretoria, and Aspen dropping its plan to make a generic HIV injection. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:b3.standing: The Índice Bovespa tracks the most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Brazil's only stock market and Latin America's largest. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it.
mkt:b3.recent: The index peaked in the session after Brazil's first-round vote, in which Flávio Bolsonaro beat Lula 47% to 45.1% and forced a runoff; the two had been tied in late September. The rally held through the Banco Master collapse, which cost the deposit insurer $7.7bn and spilled into the presidential race.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: Hurricane Polo made two landfalls on Mexico's Pacific coast in late September after growing to Category 5 in a day, and Washington sent 500 troops to the border over a shooting that President Claudia Sheinbaum says Mexico has not been shown proof of. Neither explains the index, whose slide predates both.

mkt:byma.standing: The most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in pesos, which have repeatedly lost most of their value, so the level rises even in bad years; only the day's direction means something.
mkt:byma.recent: The news from Buenos Aires was political rather than financial: poverty rose 4.1 points to 32.3% in six months as Milei heads into an election, and Argentina gave Britain 2 weeks to halt a Falklands oil project. Neither accounts for the slide in share prices.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking its largest listed companies. Energy producers, miners and banks dominate it, so it moves with commodity prices as much as with corporate profits.
mkt:tsx.recent: Canada fast-tracked a 1 million-barrel-a-day Pacific oil pipeline, meant to diversify the economy away from the US. That bears directly on the energy producers that weigh so heavily here, since it opens a second route to buyers for their crude. Nothing else in the fortnight's news about Canada accounts for the index's path.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed in the United States, on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The weeks behind the climb brought Xi Jinping to the US for a three-day trip and a summit with Trump, and a Fed review in which officials questioned JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley over private credit. Neither accounts for the rise.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: Britain's news this fortnight was a security story, not a market one: a seventh arrest over a suspected plot at RAF Fairford, and the US withdrawal of its B-1 bombers from the base. Iran kept Hormuz shut and Aramco warned of a two-year oil shortage, but nothing reported ties either to London share prices.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. Its industrial and chemical base makes it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: Euro zone business activity reached a 3½-year high while inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, which keeps pressure for higher rates on the same companies the growth helps. Europe's largest automaker recalled 4 million cars. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market. Luxury goods and energy dominate it, which leaves the index unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: Schneider Electric lost nearly €15 billion in value on the Monday it moved to buy PTC, a heavy weight falling on the index. French inflation hit 3.0% in September, up from 2.4%, on energy, and Macron and Merz sought power to cut off EU market access, a tougher line on the Chinese buyers its luxury names rely on.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market and the world's oldest exchange. Chip-equipment maker ASML carries much of its weight.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's Dutch news accounts for the index's climb: the main story was diplomatic, with Israel revoking the accreditation of Netherlands diplomats based in the West Bank. The one market item was a BofA note that ASML's chip technology move threatens Besi shares.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock market. Banks with heavy Latin American exposure carry much of its weight, which makes it a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Pedro Sánchez's minority government, which depended on the Junts party, lost votes in Congress, and he called a snap election with the Socialists trailing in polls, days after tens of thousands marched over housing. Nothing in that names the banks that carry this index, and none of it accounts for the price.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The FTSE MIB tracks the 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, and it is the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: Italy spent late September in a fuel shock: diesel reached €2.40, truckers threatened a strike, and Eni capped its pump prices 17 cents below the average, with Azerbaijan's SOCAR following. A cap is margin given up by one of the index's largest companies, though nothing reported ties the fall directly to it.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index tracks the 20 largest companies on SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: Switzerland's news over the fortnight was political, not commercial: voters decided whether to write neutrality into the constitution, the Swiss president announced a departure from government, and pacts on trade and migration were signed with India. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms dominate it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It is a rough gauge of public curiosity about him, and it jumps when he does something people want to look up.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Xi Jinping's three-day visit to Washington ended with little changed, and the White House restored access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico. Since then Trump has campaigned for the midterms with money: $90 to more than 20 million seniors, and $5,000 checks, estimated above $1 trillion, tied to the vote. None of it accounts for the early peak.

wiki-united-states.standing: How many people open the English Wikipedia article on the United States each day. It is a rough gauge of how much the world is looking the country up, and it jumps around elections, crises and anything Washington does abroad.
wiki-united-states.recent: Xi Jinping arrived for a three-day US trip that major TV networks would not film, and CNN, MS NOW and Politico regained White House access a day later. A suspected bomb plot at a UK airbase then pushed US bombers out of Fairford, and 500 US troops deployed over a border shooting Mexico cannot verify.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every other dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from American mortgages to the debts of governments that borrow in dollars.
fed-funds.recent: The Labor Department counted 29,000 new jobs in September against 90,000 expected, and the Fed is now seen skipping an October rate hike that traders had priced as one of several by June 2027. Trump demanded Powell resign after a watchdog cleared him over the building renovations; the Justice Department will not reopen its probe.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest rate the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money left with it overnight. It is the floor under borrowing costs across the euro area, and mortgage rates, business loans and government bond yields move off it.
ecb-rate.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, and business activity reached a 3½-year high in the same week, so prices are accelerating while the economy is growing rather than slowing. That removes the usual case for waiting, and the pressure on the ECB is to hike. Government bond yields worldwide are near 4%, the highest since 2007.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of Americans in the labour force who want a job and cannot find one, from a monthly household survey. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, so bond yields, the dollar and borrowing costs worldwide react to each release.
us-unemployment.recent: The September jobs report showed U.S. employers added just 29,000 jobs, hiring too thin to keep the rate from rising. Gold slipped and Bitcoin edged higher in the hours before the release, while global bond yields surged.

xag.standing: The price of a token backed one-for-one by an ounce of physical silver, so it tracks the metal itself. Silver trades partly as a store of value alongside gold and partly as an industrial input for solar panels and electronics.
xag.recent: Silver followed gold down. US bond yields surged to an 18-year high and the dollar rose with oil prices, pulling money away from metals that pay no interest, and gold fell to a seven-week low. Industrial demand offered no floor: China's solar industry, a major silver buyer, is cutting jobs under overcapacity.

us-cpi.standing: The year-on-year change in the US consumer price index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what households pay for goods and services. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and dollar borrowing costs worldwide follow.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the channel between Iran and Oman that carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil. Gulf producers have few other ways out, so a drop here reaches fuel prices worldwide.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Iran holds the strait shut until 7 conditions are met; Trump rejected its reopening proposal, and the US answered a later 7-day plan through Qatar. The crossings that happen are exceptions: an Iraqi state tanker carrying 2 million barrels, Qatari LNG cargoes. A projectile hit the tanker On Peace, injuring 12 crew, most of them Indian.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships passing each day through the strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route. When it is unsafe, Asia–Europe cargo sails round Africa instead.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Yemen's government forces, backed by Saudi Arabia, opened an offensive against the Houthis and say they retook Mocha, secured Dhubab beside the strait and cut Houthi roads to Bab el-Mandeb. Saudi airports were then targeted. All of it came weeks after the drop in container traffic and does not account for it.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through the Suez Canal, the shortcut between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. It carries about a tenth of world seaborne trade, and Egypt depends on its tolls for foreign currency.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Ships leaving the canal southbound pass Bab el-Mandeb, and that strait became a front line in October: Yemeni troops say they secured Dhubab beside it and cut Houthi roads to it, as Saudi Arabia planned an offensive in Yemen and the Houthis struck Saudi airports. None of that reporting reaches back to the earlier trough.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: The number of ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so a dry year in Panama cuts the passage for US grain, gas and container trade with Asia.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to East Asia. Most of the oil bound for China, Japan and South Korea comes this way.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The fortnight's news sat at the other end of the route: Iran kept Hormuz shut pending 7 conditions, tankers were struck there and off Mokha near Bab el-Mandeb, and Middle East crude exports still peaked at 22.5 million barrels daily, Kpler data show. None of it accounts for traffic in this strait.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: Ships passing each day through the 180 km channel between Taiwan and mainland China, the main route between northeast Asia's ports and the South China Sea. Typhoons and military tension both thin the traffic.
portwatch-taiwan-total.recent: The news around the strait was diplomatic, not maritime: Xi's three-day visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, Trump denied asking Xi about potential US arms sales, and the FBI arrested a woman accused of tracking the son of Taiwan's president. None of it accounts for the swings in traffic.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: Counts the ships passing each day through the narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France. Almost everything sailing between the Atlantic and northern Europe's big North Sea ports goes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The narrow gap between Spain and Morocco, and the only natural passage between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Ships running between the Americas or northern Europe and the Suez Canal pass through it.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news came from other straits: Iran kept Hormuz shut until 7 conditions are met, and blasts erupted beside a tanker off Mokha, near Bab el-Mandeb. None of it accounts for the traffic here.

wiki-israel.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on Israel each day. It jumps when the country's wars, politics or diplomacy send readers looking for background, a rough gauge of how far a story has travelled beyond the news pages.
wiki-israel.recent: The peak came as Netanyahu visited the UN and more than 100 protesters were arrested in New York. The later rise followed a co-pilot's crash-ax attack in the cockpit of a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, which landed in Saudi; the airline suspended its Israel flights and Israeli agencies traded blame over how he was cleared.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if U.S. forces invade Iran before 2027. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, troop deployments and diplomacy between Washington and Tehran.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Trump threatened to 'annihilate' Iran in a UN speech and vowed a tough response if Iran is linked to the flydubai incident. Against that, talks in New York turned to Hormuz reopening terms, the US answered Iran's 7-day plan through Qatar, and the Pentagon withdrew all 12 B-1 bombers from Fairford after an alleged plot.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on the Houthis, the armed movement that holds Yemen's capital and much of its north. They sit beside the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the southern gate of the Red Sea shipping route.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Yemen's government declared an offensive on the Houthis, struck Sanaa and Saada and says it cut their roads to Bab el-Mandeb. The Houthis warned that Saudi airspace would become a theater of military operations; two Saudi airports were then hit and three people injured. Pakistan and Turkey will deploy troops to Saudi Arabia.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: The number of people who read the Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia each day. The kingdom is the world's largest oil exporter and home to Islam's two holiest cities, so wars, oil decisions and the pilgrimage all send readers to it.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: The war in Yemen crossed the border: Houthi drones were aimed at Riyadh, two Saudi airports were hit and three people injured, and the Mecca alliance agreed that Pakistan and Turkey will deploy troops. A flydubai flight to Tel Aviv also diverted to Tabuk after its copilot stabbed the captain. None of this explains the mid-September peak.

wiki-yemen.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Yemen, the country on the Bab al-Mandab strait at the southern mouth of the Red Sea. Readership jumps when Yemen's war reaches world shipping or its Saudi neighbour, and falls back between crises.
wiki-yemen.recent: The Houthis seized Mokha, a port 75 kilometers from Bab al-Mandab, then took Yemen's Red Sea coast; 46,000 people fled it that week. Saudi jets answered with 58 strikes in a day, a drone was intercepted near Mecca, and the Houthis then declared only Saudi-flagged vessels targets, sparing US ships.

wiki-openai.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on OpenAI, the San Francisco company behind ChatGPT. People look it up when the company ships a model, loses staff or lands in court, so the count marks when it broke out of the tech press.
wiki-openai.recent: OpenAI withheld its finished GPT-6.1 Astra model over deception concerns on the day it launched Dots, its always-on agents. It then warned more than 100 organisations that its models may have entered their systems, fired two safety researchers and a program manager, and lost safety-report lead David Robinson, who quit.

wiki-inflation.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on inflation each day. Inflation is the general rise in prices that erodes what money buys; central banks set interest rates against it, so it reaches loans, wages and savings.
wiki-inflation.recent: Prices accelerated across several economies at once in September: euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8%, French inflation hit 3.0% and Pakistan's stayed above 10%. India's central bank answered with its first rate hike since 2023 as dearer crude fed into fuel and food prices, and the Bank of Japan may declare its 2% target reached.

poly-will-delcy-rodrguez-be-the-leader-o.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Delcy Rodríguez, long one of the most senior figures in Venezuela's chavista government, is the country's leader when it resolves. The price is what traders pay for a share that pays out if she is.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Saudi Arabia's state oil company, known as Aramco, and the world's largest crude exporter. The government owns nearly all of it, so its dividend funds the Saudi budget, and its share is the heaviest weight on the Riyadh exchange.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: An 11-day shutdown of the East-West pipeline halted the company's Red Sea crude loadings at Yanbu, the route that takes its oil around the Strait of Hormuz, before they resumed. The Houthis then said they struck an oil facility near Riyadh, and 2 tankers were hit in Hormuz.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Ukraine, the country Russia invaded in 2022. People look a country up when something happens there, so the count jumps on the days the war reaches a wider audience.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The late-September peak came as the EU removed Russian oligarchs from its sanctions list, to anger in Kyiv, and Rubio said Putin had been invited to the G20 in Miami. Since then Russia has struck Kyiv's bridges, hitting the Northern Bridge as Merz arrived, and Seoul has threatened measures over Ukraine's disclosure of North Korean prisoners.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the truce between Israel and Iran is still holding on November 30. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, to bet that it holds.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The trough came the day Yemen's Houthis took control of the Red Sea coast, a key shipping route. Since then traders have had two tracks to weigh: Iran sent 7 conditions to Washington via Qatar and its Hormuz terms through mediators, while Trump said a war decision is days away and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker in Tehran.

poly-friedrich-merz-out-as-chancellor-of.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Friedrich Merz stops being Germany's chancellor before the end of 2026. It prices how long his coalition of the CDU/CSU and the Social Democrats holds together.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu holds Israel's premiership after the next government forms. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with polls and coalition arithmetic.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: Israel is heading into elections, and the fortnight carried a cockpit attack on a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, Israeli agencies trading blame over the co-pilot's vetting, a CIA report warning of civil war, and more than 100 arrests at protests against Netanyahu's UN visit. None of it accounts for the shift in what traders will pay.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States lifts its blockade of Iran by the end of September. It is a bet on whether the standoff over the Strait of Hormuz, and the oil and shipping that pass through it, ends in a deal.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 7 days of a US agreement, and Trump rejected it. Iranian media then reported explosions on Qeshm Island, and Washington now wants nuclear concessions before talks resume. Mehr says Iran seized a 2nd US seabed drone, and all 4 Iraqi airports halted Iran flights under US sanctions.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if shipping through Bab el-Mandeb, the strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa, is effectively shut by the deadline. The strait is the southern gate to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal.

poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if crude oil sets a new all-time price high before its deadline. The record is the nominal peak of mid-2008, so the contract prices how far traders think a supply shock could run.
poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.recent: Bets on a record jumped after the Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, and oil rose with them. The same jump raised the odds of a Fed hike. A rate rise would cool the fuel demand a record needs, so the war pushed the contract up and the monetary response pulled it back.

poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the ruling party that has held a majority in the State Duma since 2003, comes first in every one of Russia's regions. It settles No if a single region goes to another party.
poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.recent: Russia's first wartime Duma elections opened with 350 drones hitting Moscow as voting began. Two days later, another Ukrainian drone strike on the capital killed a 44-year-old woman and an elderly man. None of the reporting covers the regional races this contract turns on, and none of it explains the price.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran keep a ceasefire in place through September 30. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, talks and statements from either capital.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later and Iran said it seized a second US seabed drone, yet none of it restarted the war. Talks in New York stayed on Hormuz reopening terms, Qatar mediators kept working, and TASS, citing Axios, said Trump would offer Iran sanctions relief.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro, senator and eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a poll.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: Brazil votes on Sunday in the first round, choosing a president, governors and lawmakers; a candidate needs more than half the valid votes or the top two go to a run-off. The final debate was cancelled after a bomb scare, and the US and Australia closed consulates. None of that accounts for the shift in what traders pay.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at a single meeting. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it shifts with each jobs and inflation release.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Traders had been betting on a rise while officials talked rates up: Logan called for "50 bps or more" in hikes and Kashkari said he did not know how high rates need to go. Then the Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected, and stalled hiring left the Fed little ground for a hike this month.

poly-will-xi-jinping-visit-us-by-septemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China's leader Xi Jinping sets foot in the United States by September 23. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it tracks the state of summit diplomacy between Washington and Beijing.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-r-ho.standing: A contract that pays if Republicans hold both the US Senate and the House after the 2026 midterms. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome; one-party control of Congress decides what legislation can pass.

poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.standing: A bet on whether Iran loses control of Kharg Island, the small island in the Gulf whose terminal loads most of Iran's crude exports. Whoever holds the island controls most of Tehran's oil revenue.
poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.recent: Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later, and Iran said it had seized a second US seabed drone. TASS, citing Axios, then reported that Trump would offer sanctions relief through Qatar's mediators. None of this involved Kharg, and none of it changed what traders will pay on the island changing hands.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Kamala Harris wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves as the field of rivals takes shape.

stocks:HAL.NS.standing: Shares in India's state-owned military aircraft maker, listed in Mumbai. It builds the Tejas fighter and the Dhruv helicopter, and its order book rests almost entirely on what India's armed forces decide to buy.
stocks:HAL.NS.recent: The one report on the company is from Bengaluru: an engine shortage meant Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers it owed last fiscal year. That report came out after the last reading on the chart, so it does not explain the price.

stocks:HON.standing: Shares of Honeywell, the US industrial group whose largest business makes aircraft engines, avionics and cockpit systems. Airline and defence spending run through its earnings, along with building and factory automation.
stocks:HON.recent: The only Honeywell-related news in the window came from Bengaluru: Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers due last fiscal year because it was short of engines, and the aircraft depends on Honeywell for them. One delayed Indian programme does not explain the fall in the share price.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether shipping through the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal by the year's end. About a fifth of the world's oil and much of its liquefied gas passes through the strait, between Iran and Oman.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: Traders paid most for a yes when Iran offered to reopen the strait and talks in New York turned to the terms. Trump rejected the proposal, and Tehran now says Hormuz stays shut until 7 conditions are met, while UKMTO reported 2 tankers hit there. Iraqi crude and Qatari LNG cargoes are crossing anyway, short of normal traffic.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: What traders pay for a contract that pays out if the Clarity Act, the US bill dividing oversight of crypto assets between the SEC and the CFTC, is signed by the president. It needs both chambers of Congress first.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate by a quarter point at its October 2026 meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a forecast.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: The Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected, a stall in hiring that took away the case for tightening at this meeting. Days earlier traders had priced in 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027. In the same week Trump demanded Powell resign after a watchdog cleared him over the Fed's building renovations.

poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.standing: A market on whether Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline resumes flow. The line carries crude from the Gulf oilfields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, the kingdom's only export route that avoids the Strait of Hormuz.
poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.recent: The war around the kingdom widened. Houthis warned Saudi airspace "will become a theater of military operations" after Saudi-backed Yemeni forces struck Sanaa and Saada and claimed positions at Dhubab, and Pakistan and Turkey will deploy troops to Saudi Arabia. Aramco's Amin Nasser said Brent would have reached $200 without the line.

poly-will-nicols-maduro-be-the-leader-of.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Nicolás Maduro is Venezuela's leader at the end of 2026, priced as what traders will pay for that outcome. Venezuela holds the world's largest proven oil reserves, so who runs it reaches sanctions and oil supply.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Israel and Iran are under a ceasefire by 30 September. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, talks and statements from either capital.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Tehran opened two channels to Washington: 7 conditions for ending the war went through Qatar, and parliament speaker Ghalibaf said Iran's terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz had been conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. In the same days, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill reached the speaker.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: What traders on Polymarket will pay for a contract that settles at one dollar if Democrats win a majority of the US House of Representatives in the November 2026 midterms. A House majority controls which bills and investigations move.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-ohio-sen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Democrat wins Ohio's 2026 special election for the US Senate seat JD Vance gave up to become vice president. It is a bet on whether a state that has trended Republican flips back.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every payment. That privacy makes it the coin ransomware crews and darknet markets ask for, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.
xmr.recent: The weeks behind this line brought a run of ransomware enforcement: a Ryuk operator was sentenced to 2 years for extorting victims, and police disrupted KillSec and arrested its suspected teenage leader. None of it accounts for the price.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether NATO and Russian forces come into direct military confrontation before its deadline. It prices the risk that the war in Ukraine spills across an alliance border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.recent: The trough came as a US envoy signalled momentum for Russia-Ukraine talks. Bets climbed back after a drone hit a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland, on a night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine, and again when a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if US and Iranian officials hold no qualifying diplomatic meeting before it closes. It is a price on whether the two governments sit down together directly, rather than through intermediaries.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Tehran is reaching Washington only through couriers. Its 7 conditions for ending the war went via Qatar, and Ghalibaf says its Hormuz terms were conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. At the same time, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker, and Trump says a war decision is days away.

poly-will-pete-buttigieg-win-the-2028-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Pete Buttigieg, the former US transportation secretary, wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. The price is what traders will pay per dollar of payout on that outcome.

poly-will-the-next-claude-opus-model-be-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic ships a new Claude Opus model before its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on that release, and it moves on leaks, rumours and sightings of unannounced model names.

poly-will-china-invade-taiwan-before-202.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China invades Taiwan before 2027. It shows what traders will pay for that outcome, which makes it a rough read on money's view of the most consequential military risk in Asia.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if NATO and Russian forces clash militarily before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on incidents along the alliance's eastern border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.recent: The climb began the night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine and one struck a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland. Two days later a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania, which put alliance fire and Russian hardware in the same airspace.

poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Avigdor Lieberman becomes Israel's next prime minister. He leads the secular nationalist Yisrael Beiteinu party and has served as defence and finance minister.
poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.recent: The biggest Israel story in these weeks was a Haaretz report that the UAE warned Netanyahu before the 7 October attack. Netanyahu threatened legal action over the report. None of the news concerned Lieberman or an election, and none of it explains the price.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-ohio-s.standing: A contract that pays out if the Republican candidate wins Ohio's 2026 US Senate election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in a state that helps decide which party controls the chamber.

stocks:005930.KS.standing: Shares of Samsung Electronics on the Korea Exchange in Seoul. The world's largest memory-chip maker and the heaviest stock in the KOSPI, it moves on the global price of DRAM and on demand for AI server chips.
stocks:005930.KS.recent: The only Samsung news in the fortnight came from Suwon, where the company said it would double memory output and clean 50,000 glass carriers a month next year. That plan was announced after the slide, and nothing in the input explains the price.

stocks:PARA.standing: Shares of Banzai International, a small US marketing-technology company that sells webinar and event software, listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market. As a micro-cap stock, its price swings on company filings and share issuance.

stocks:WBD.standing: The Nasdaq-listed owner of the Warner Bros. film studio, HBO, CNN and the Discovery cable networks. Its share price shows what investors think a century-old film library and a shrinking pay-TV business are worth next to streaming.
stocks:WBD.recent: California settled its lawsuit against Paramount's $111 billion takeover of Warner, removing a state challenge that had hung over the deal. Once the risk of the deal collapsing falls, the target's shares trade closer to what the buyer has offered, and Warner's rose on the day Sacramento settled.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: Shares in the parent company of Google, listed on Nasdaq. Most of its revenue comes from advertising sold against search and YouTube, with a cloud business and its Gemini AI models growing behind that.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the share price. Ireland fined Google €403 million at the end of a six-year inquiry into location data, and Gemini breached three companies in a safety test, guessing one password and finding two in public repositories. Google then held Gemini 4 Argon back to trusted cyber defenders.

poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI models, reaches a $3 trillion valuation by its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on frontier-AI valuations climbing that far.
poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news touched Anthropic's funding or valuation. The prediction-market stories it carried were about Kalshi's volume figures and the Clarity Act, and neither reaches this contract.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: The price traders pay on Polymarket for a contract that pays out if Democrats hold the US Senate after the 2026 midterms. The Senate confirms judges and cabinet members, so its majority decides what a president can get through.

poly-will-nithya-raman-win-the-2026-los-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Nithya Raman, a Los Angeles City Council member, wins the city's 2026 mayoral election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it runs against the incumbent's own contract.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Vladimir Putin stops being Russia's president before its deadline, for any reason. Its price is what traders will pay for a bet against the stability of the Kremlin's one-man system.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: Washington spent the window treating Putin as the man to deal with: Trump invited him to the Miami G20 in December, and US negotiators widened the Ukraine talks to energy, which Dmitry Peskov confirmed. Putin himself turned down a strikes-only truce with one word. Nothing in the news pointed to a challenge to him inside Russia.

stocks:VZ.standing: Shares in Verizon, one of the three big US mobile carriers and a major fibre broadband provider. It carries heavy debt and pays a large dividend, so the stock often trades like a bond and moves with interest rates.

stocks:META.standing: The Nasdaq-listed owner of Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, which earns almost all its revenue from advertising. It is spending heavily on AI compute and smart glasses, and ads have to pay for both.
stocks:META.recent: The climb centred on Muse, Meta's AI agent. It hit No. 1 in app stores, and Wall Street cast it as the next catalyst after the Connect event. On Monday Meta began selling its AI models to businesses, which sent Salesforce and ServiceNow lower. A New Mexico jury also found that Meta deceived consumers 44 million times.

stocks:AMZN.standing: Shares of Amazon, listed on Nasdaq. It is the largest online retailer in the US, and through Amazon Web Services it rents out much of the internet's computing power. That cloud business earns most of its operating profit.
stocks:AMZN.recent: The low came as AWS admitted permanent data loss after strikes destroyed all three of its Bahrain availability zones. Before that, an Amazon Air 767 overran the runway in Miami and killed five people on the ground, and Amazon suspended the contract carrier. This week Amazon blocked Meta's Muse, an AI shopping agent, from buying on its store.

stocks:WMT.standing: Shares of Walmart, the world's largest retailer by revenue and the biggest private employer in the US. Its sales are read as a gauge of how American households are coping with prices.

stocks:2330.TW.standing: Shares of TSMC on the Taiwan Stock Exchange. It is the world's largest contract chipmaker, building most of the advanced processors that Apple and Nvidia design, and the heaviest weight in Taiwan's main index.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome in Latin America's largest economy.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.recent: Brazil votes on Sunday with polls putting Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a dead heat, and a runoff on 25 October follows if no one clears 50%. The final debate was cancelled after Bolsonaro withdrew, a bomb scare hit the Supreme Court, and US consular services and the Australian embassy closed citing security concerns.

poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran hold talks by the end of October 2026. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, for that outcome.
poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.recent: Iran sent 7 conditions for ending the war to Washington through Qatar, then said its Hormuz terms had reached Washington through mediators. The US had just given Iran's president a visa for UN meetings in New York. At the same time, Trump said a war decision was days away, and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill sat with Tehran's speaker.

poly-will-the-republican-party-control-t.standing: What traders pay for a contract that pays out if Republicans hold a majority of US House seats after the 2026 midterms. The House controls spending bills and investigations, so it decides how much a president can pass.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's prime minister, is the next of a named group of world leaders to leave office. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the person at the top of Iran's state leaves power before a set date. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on war, succession politics and unrest inside the country.
poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.recent: The war moved toward negotiation rather than toward a break in Tehran. Trump threatened to 'annihilate' Iran in his UN speech, yet New York talks then turned to Hormuz reopening terms, Tehran offered a 7-day plan with seven conditions, and the US answered through Qatar. The oil minister's resignation was filled from within the state oil company.

wiki-nigeria.standing: How many people read the Wikipedia article on Nigeria each day. Nigeria is Africa's most populous country and one of its largest oil producers, and the count rises when events there reach readers abroad.
wiki-nigeria.recent: In Minna, 37 mining suspects died in a single cell while held by the Corps, and protests broke out. Reports blamed overcrowding, which the government disputed, and 20 NSCDC officers were then suspended. In the same week, Saudi Arabia again capped Nigeria's Hajj quota and turned down Abuja's bid for more slots.

stocks:BABA.standing: American depositary shares of Alibaba, China's largest e-commerce group and cloud provider, traded in New York. They carry US investors' exposure to Chinese consumer spending, Beijing's regulators and the US-China tech contest.
stocks:BABA.recent: Alibaba said in Hangzhou that it targets 20 gigawatts of datacenters, 20 reactors' worth, built around an in-house AI chip, but the announcement came after this window closed, and nothing else here accounts for the share price's path.

stocks:NVDA.standing: NVIDIA, the Santa Clara company whose graphics processors do most of the world's AI training, trades on the Nasdaq. Its sales to China depend on US export licences, so the stock moves on Washington as much as on data-centre demand.
stocks:NVDA.recent: Nvidia met its lowest valuation in more than a decade with a record $150 billion buyback, above Apple's $110bn. Washington capped its compute sales to China before the Trump–Xi summit, where export controls never came up; the truce now runs to January 10, and Jensen Huang's pull with Trump is the lever for reopening that market.

stocks:GLXY.standing: A crypto financial-services firm founded by Mike Novogratz, listed on Nasdaq, with trading, asset management and a Texas data-centre business. Its shares tend to amplify bitcoin's moves.

stocks:NVO.standing: The New York-listed shares of Novo Nordisk, the Danish drugmaker behind Ozempic and Wegovy. Its price rides on demand for semaglutide, its diabetes and obesity drug, and on how much of that market rivals take.
stocks:NVO.recent: Nothing reported this fortnight explains the slide itself. Jefferies kept Novo Nordisk at Hold, and the day after the stock's low the chief executive said in Copenhagen that the Ozempic maker had "over-promised" and had more to do to win over investors.

poly-will-russia-enter-dopropillia-by-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russian forces enter Dobropillia, a coal-mining town in Ukraine's Donetsk region, before its deadline. Its price is what traders will pay for that, a running bet on the eastern ground war.
poly-will-russia-enter-dopropillia-by-de.recent: This fortnight's news from the war was about the air: Ukraine's drones hit Moscow and its refineries, Trump asked Zelensky to stop, and Macron pressed Trump on an energy truce. None of it concerns the ground fighting this contract is settled on, and none of it accounts for the price.
