poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline is flowing again by Sep 30. The line carries crude from the eastern oil fields to Yanbu on the Red Sea, the kingdom's route for oil that avoids the Strait of Hormuz.
poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.recent: Attacks on the pipeline in mid-month raised the prospect of oil at its highest in months. Word of a restart then pushed Brent below $98, but the fighting widened. France sent soldiers and radars to guard Yanbu, the UK committed an RAF tanker to refuel Saudi jets striking the Houthis, and Saudi defences downed Houthi drones aimed at Riyadh.

poly-will-jean-luc-mlenchon-win-the-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Jean-Luc Mélenchon, founder of the left-wing La France Insoumise, wins France's 2027 presidential election. He has run three times and narrowly missed the runoff in 2022.

poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-us-p.standing: The price of a Polymarket contract that pays out if Gavin Newsom, the California Democrat, wins the 2028 US presidential election. It is what traders are betting, and it moves on primary polling, endorsements and rivals' entries.

poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-sep.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if US and Iranian officials meet by 30 September 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with the messages mediators carry between the two governments.
poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-sep.recent: The rebound from mid-September followed Tehran's first written terms: seven conditions for ending the war sent to Washington through Qatar, and Hormuz terms passed on by mediators. Trump has talked of meeting Iranian officials at the UN, yet told the same assembly he could "annihilate" Iran.

poly-will-mary-peltola-win-the-alaska-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Mary Peltola, the Democrat who once held Alaska's lone House seat, wins the state's US Senate race. Alaska has not sent a Democrat to the Senate since 2008.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the ceasefire between the United States and Iran is still in force on its end date. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with the risk to Gulf oil and shipping.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Trump threatened to 'annihilate' Iran in his UN speech, and the contract traded at its cheapest. Talks in New York on Hormuz reopening terms turned it, and the US answered Iran's 7-day plan through Qatar. Buyers kept paying as the US pulled its B-1 bombers from Fairford over an alleged plot and Tehran debated quitting the nuclear treaty.

poly-will-russia-enter-sloviansk-by-dece.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russian forces enter Sloviansk, a city in Ukraine's Donetsk region. With neighbouring Kramatorsk, it anchors the largest urban belt Kyiv has held there through the war.
poly-will-russia-enter-sloviansk-by-dece.recent: The fortnight's news about the war was fought in the air and over energy, not on the ground. Ukrainian drones set a Moscow refinery alight, Trump pressed Kyiv to stop refinery strikes as Macron floated an energy truce, and the EU and Washington funded weapons and air defence. None of it concerns fighting near Sloviansk or explains the price.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.standing: What traders on Polymarket will pay for a contract that settles at $1 if JD Vance, the US vice-president, wins the 2028 presidential election. It prices the Republican succession years before any primary vote is cast.

poly-will-franois-hollande-win-the-2027-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if François Hollande, France's Socialist president from 2012 to 2017, wins the 2027 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in cents on the dollar.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Marco Rubio wins the Republican nomination for president in 2028. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it shifts as the field of rivals for the nomination forms.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A contract on whether shipping through Bab el-Mandeb, the strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa, effectively stops by a deadline. It is the southern gate to the Red Sea and Suez, the short route between Asia and Europe.

poly-will-david-lisnard-win-the-2027-fre.standing: What traders on Polymarket will pay for a contract that pays out if David Lisnard, the conservative mayor of Cannes, wins France's 2027 presidential election. It prices one contender for the mainstream right's vote against the rest of the field.

poly-will-naftali-bennett-be-the-next-pr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Naftali Bennett, who unseated Benjamin Netanyahu in 2021 at the head of a broad coalition, becomes Israel's next prime minister. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome.
poly-will-naftali-bennett-be-the-next-pr.recent: The fortnight's Israeli headlines centred on a Haaretz report that the UAE warned Netanyahu of a Hamas plan days before 7 October, which he threatened legal action over, and on 12 countries moving to sanction settlement trade. None of it concerned Bennett or an election date, and none of it accounts for the price.

poly-will-yulia-navalnaya-win-the-nobel-.standing: A contract that pays out if the Norwegian Nobel Committee awards the Peace Prize to Yulia Navalnaya, who took up the leadership of Russia's exiled opposition after her husband Alexei Navalny died in an Arctic prison.

poly-will-russia-enter-kramatorsk-by-dec.standing: A contract that pays out if Russian forces enter Kramatorsk by the end of 2026. The city became Ukraine's administrative seat for Donetsk after 2014 and, with Sloviansk, anchors the last urban belt Kyiv holds in the region.
poly-will-russia-enter-kramatorsk-by-dec.recent: The fortnight's news from the war centred elsewhere: Trump pressing Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refineries, Macron pressing him on an energy truce, and a $2.68 billion US air-defence sale awaiting Congress. None of it concerned the ground fighting around Kramatorsk.

poly-will-trump-and-putin-not-meet-432.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin do not meet in person before its deadline. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves on summit talk and on Ukraine ceasefire diplomacy.
poly-will-trump-and-putin-not-meet-432.recent: The fortnight's reporting on Russia centred on the EU delisting Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman to keep its sanctions regime alive; nothing in it concerns a Trump–Putin meeting or accounts for traders shifting their bets.

poly-will-josh-shapiro-win-the-2028-demo.standing: A contract that pays out if Josh Shapiro, elected governor of Pennsylvania in 2022, becomes the Democratic nominee for president in 2028. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, not a poll.

stocks:ORCL.standing: The Austin-based maker of the Oracle database and business software such as PeopleSoft, now spending heavily to build cloud data centres for AI customers. Its share price tracks how investors judge that debt-funded buildout.
stocks:ORCL.recent: The slide coincided with a fortnight of Oracle trouble: filings showed Larry Ellison had pledged 346 million shares, worth $50 billion, as loan collateral; Oracle was found liable to pay investors in its Doña Ana County data centre even if power never arrives; and ShinyHunters restarted attacks by exploiting PeopleSoft's own patch workaround.

stocks:MSFT.standing: The share price of Microsoft, maker of Windows and Office and owner of the Azure cloud, listed on Nasdaq. It is one of the world's most valuable companies, and investors watch it for what businesses spend on cloud computing and AI.
stocks:MSFT.recent: The news about Microsoft in these weeks was about security and AI. A Patch Tuesday release fixed 973 vulnerabilities, and CISA warned that two were being exploited. Court filings quoted a Microsoft executive calling AI scraping "the largest theft of labor in human history". None of it accounts for the share price.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States lifts its blockade of Iran by the deadline in its title. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each turn in the talks over the Strait of Hormuz.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Traders paid most while talks in New York worked through terms for reopening Hormuz. Then came a suspected bomb plot at a UK airbase used by the US, and Trump vowed a tough response over a flydubai incident. Tehran now says Hormuz stays shut until 7 conditions are met, and the US has answered its 7-day plan through Qatar.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-us-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Kamala Harris wins the 2028 US presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with her standing among possible Democratic candidates.
poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-us-.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news touches the 2028 race or accounts for the change in what traders are paying. The story was the venue itself: New York sued Polymarket for illegal gambling, saying it lets 18-to-20-year-olds bet where state law sets 21.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Shares of Apple, the Cupertino company that makes the iPhone, traded on Nasdaq. It is one of the largest companies in the world by market value, so its moves carry heavy weight in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100.
stocks:AAPL.recent: Apple shipped a rebuilt Siri in iOS 27 as the iPhone 18 reached stores at higher prices. The UK made it pull its strongest iCloud encryption for new users. A San Diego jury then awarded Taction Technology $5.72 billion over a haptics patent. None of these reports connects any of it to the share price.

wiki-pakistan.standing: How many times a day the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan is opened. It rises when the nuclear-armed country of some 240 million, bordering Afghanistan, India, Iran and China, draws readers from outside it.
wiki-pakistan.recent: Pakistan struck what it called drone launchpads inside Afghanistan, and two days later a suicide bomber killed 12 at a police checkpoint in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. At home, Imran Khan's sister was arrested before a Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf march on Islamabad set for 4 October, which the army has warned it will meet with force.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-maine-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Republican wins Maine's 2026 US Senate race, for the seat Susan Collins holds. Maine leans Democratic in presidential races and counts its Senate ballots by ranked choice.

poly-will-dan-sullivan-win-the-alaska-se.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Dan Sullivan, Alaska's Republican US senator, wins his seat's election. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves on polling, candidate news and control of the Senate.

poly-variational-fdv-above-1b-one-day-af.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the token of Variational, a crypto derivatives trading platform, is valued at $1 billion or more when it launches. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which makes it a live read on appetite for new crypto tokens.

poly-will-the-price-of-bitcoin-be-betwee.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if bitcoin settles between $84,000 and $86,000 on its resolution date. It is one rung in a ladder of adjacent price bands, so its price shows where bettors are putting money along that ladder.
poly-will-the-price-of-bitcoin-be-betwee.recent: The news on bitcoin this fortnight pointed lower: it sank to $77,000 as CPI landed with hike odds near 70%, then slipped again as Clarity Act odds faded when Republicans rejected Democrats' counter-proposal. Nothing reported from the days this band gained explains why bettors moved into it.

stocks:NET.standing: Shares of Cloudflare, whose network sits in front of a large share of the world's websites and handles their traffic, DNS and attack filtering. When it goes down, much of the web goes down with it.

stocks:VLKAF.standing: Volkswagen's shares as traded over the counter in the US, in dollars. The Wolfsburg group owns VW, Audi, Škoda and most of Porsche, and as Europe's largest carmaker it carries the region's exposure to the electric transition.
stocks:VLKAF.recent: Volkswagen wrote down $11.5 billion, mostly on Porsche, as Germany's carmakers cut jobs. Days earlier Handelsblatt reported that Porsche could face another 4,000 job cuts. The group also lost Škoda chief Klaus Zellmer, whom Volvo Cars appointed as CEO to lead a turnaround.

stocks:MBGYY.standing: The US over-the-counter dollar quote for Mercedes-Benz Group, the Stuttgart maker of premium cars and vans. China is one of its largest markets, so Chinese demand and EU and US trade rules drive its profits.
stocks:MBGYY.recent: The only related report in these weeks was the EU's August registrations, in which electric cars took 27.7% of sales. It names no carmaker and does not explain the fall in the share price.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-republic.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if J.D. Vance becomes the Republican presidential nominee in 2028. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in a race where the sitting vice-president starts as the name to beat.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-d-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays if the 2026 midterms leave Republicans running the Senate and Democrats the House. That split would give House Democrats subpoena power and a block on legislation, while confirmations stay Republican.
poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-d-ho.recent: The fortnight's prediction-market news concerned the venue, not the races: New York sued Polymarket as an illegal gambling operation for letting 18-to-20-year-olds bet where state law sets 21. Nothing reported about the Senate or House contests accounts for the price.

poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-demo.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Gavin Newsom, the California Democrat, becomes his party's nominee for US president in 2028. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, long before any primary vote is cast.
poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-demo.recent: The fortnight's news was about the venue, not the candidate: New York sued Polymarket for letting 18-to-20-year-olds bet where state law sets 21, and an appeals court ruled that states can regulate Kalshi's sports contracts. None of it accounts for the shift in what traders pay for Newsom.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-finis.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the Workers' Party leader who has won Brazil's presidency three times, places second in the 2026 election. Its price is what traders will pay for him losing first place.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-nebras.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays a dollar if a Republican wins Nebraska's 2026 US Senate race. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome. Nebraska last elected a Democratic senator in 2006.

poly-will-save-the-children-win-the-nobe.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Save the Children, the children's charity founded in London in 1919, is named Nobel Peace Prize laureate. The Norwegian Nobel Committee announces the prize in Oslo each October.

wiki-european-union.standing: A political and economic union of 27 European countries that share a single market and a common trade policy, and most of them a currency. Its rules on competition, data and product standards bind firms far beyond its borders.
wiki-european-union.recent: EU chief von der Leyen proposed an "associate member" status for Canada, a category no EU treaty defines, and Mark Carney spoke in Strasbourg the next day; soon after, Ottawa's own Brussels envoy played the label down. The same week the Commission set 13 and 15 as EU-wide minimum ages for social media.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.standing: A contract that pays out if Democrats win both the Senate and the House in the 2026 US midterm elections. Control of both chambers decides whether a president's legislation, budgets and nominees get through Congress.
poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.recent: The news of the past fortnight was about the venue, not the race: New York sued Polymarket for taking bets from 18-to-20-year-olds where state law sets 21, and an appeals court ruled that states can regulate Kalshi's sports contracts. Neither accounts for the shift in what traders will pay for this outcome.

poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve gets through 2026 without lowering its benchmark interest rate even once. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on inflation data and Fed signals.
poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.recent: The Fed raised rates on a 12-0 vote and blamed a supply shock from a closed strait. Goldman Sachs had dropped its no-hike call days earlier, and the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5%. After that hike, and with traders pricing in 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027, very few wanted to bet on a cut before year-end.

wiki-united-nations-general-assembly.standing: The Wikipedia article on the one UN body where every member state has a seat and an equal vote. Readers arrive each September, when leaders gather in New York for the general debate.
wiki-united-nations-general-assembly.recent: Trump used his speech in New York to threaten to "annihilate" Iran and to reject UN oversight of AI, while Iranian officials held three hours of direct talks with Witkoff on reopening Hormuz. Guterres warned that Israel's settlements raise "the spectre of ethnic cleansing", and nearly 70 delegations walked out when Netanyahu spoke.

poly-will-jon-ossoff-win-the-2028-us-pre.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Jon Ossoff, the Democratic senator from Georgia, wins the 2028 US presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a forecast of it.

stocks:TSLA.standing: Shares of Tesla, the US electric-car maker run by Elon Musk. Its valuation rests far more on bets about self-driving and robotics than on the cars it sells, so the stock swings on Musk's promises as much as on deliveries.
stocks:TSLA.recent: The fortnight's news on Tesla was about what comes after the cars: Musk set Oct. 1 for the long-delayed Roadster, Fremont workers balked at training the Optimus humanoid robots meant to replace them, and Kalshi sought 24/7 perpetual contracts on Tesla and Nvidia. None of it accounts for the share price.

poly-will-jon-ossoff-win-the-2028-democr.standing: What traders pay on Polymarket for a contract that settles at a dollar if Jon Ossoff, a Democratic senator from Georgia, is the party's 2028 presidential nominee. It moves on polls, endorsements and rivals' entries.

stocks:COIN.standing: Shares of Coinbase Global, the largest US-listed cryptocurrency exchange. Its revenue rides on trading volumes and on interest from USDC reserves it shares with Circle, so the stock moves with crypto prices and Washington's rules.
stocks:COIN.recent: The slide began when the Senate rejected the Clarity Act, the crypto market-structure bill, and Coinbase fell nearly 9% in a day. The rebound followed the SEC's five-year exemption for tokenized stocks, a business analysts said Coinbase, Robinhood and Circle stand to gain from.

stocks:BA.standing: America's largest aerospace company and one half of the global duopoly in large passenger jets, alongside Airbus. Its shares move on 737 delivery rates, safety findings and regulator scrutiny, and on US defence contracts.
stocks:BA.recent: The news on Boeing this fortnight was about safety. A 737 turned back after a mid-air emergency in Iran, and Boeing then flagged a 737 MAX glitch that its own cockpit software update created, which can make an automated navigation feature fail during landing. The glitch came out after the last close shown, so it does not explain the slide.

stocks:LUV.standing: Shares of Southwest Airlines, the Dallas-based US carrier, traded on the New York Stock Exchange. It flies only Boeing 737s, so the stock answers to Boeing's deliveries and safety record as well as to jet fuel and fares.
stocks:LUV.recent: The one relevant story landed the day after the peak: Boeing said its own software update had created a landing fault on the 737 MAX, the jet Southwest's fleet is built around. It came too late to explain the climb before it, and nothing in the input accounts for that rise.

poly-will-alexandria-ocasio-cortez-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, moving on polls, endorsements and signals about a run.
poly-will-alexandria-ocasio-cortez-win-t.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news touched Ocasio-Cortez or the nomination race, and none of it accounts for the price. The stories were about the venue itself: New York sued Polymarket for letting 18-to-20-year-olds bet where state law sets 21, and the Sixth Circuit ruled that states can regulate Kalshi's sports contracts.

stocks:UAL.standing: The parent company of United Airlines, one of the largest US carriers, with hubs in Chicago, Denver, Houston, Newark and San Francisco. Its shares move with jet fuel costs and demand for business and long-haul travel.
stocks:UAL.recent: The fortnight's main aviation news was Boeing's disclosure that its own software update created a landing fault on the 737 MAX, but nothing reported in the period accounts for the move in the share price.

wiki-xi-jinping.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on Xi Jinping, who has led China's Communist Party and armed forces since 2012 and its state since 2013. It jumps when he meets a US president or moves against his own elite.
wiki-xi-jinping.recent: Xi's first state visit to the US since 2015 opened on 23 September. It ended with the trade truce extended to January 10, $30bn in tariff cuts and a joint pledge to keep AI under human control. Xi also pressed Trump to change one word in US Taiwan policy. The visit came days after a purge left his own military commission with just two members.

stocks:AXISBANK.NS.standing: One of India's largest private-sector lenders, listed on the National Stock Exchange in Mumbai. Its shares follow Indian credit growth, retail and corporate lending, and the rate outlook set by the Reserve Bank of India.
stocks:AXISBANK.NS.recent: Indian bank unions called a three-day nationwide strike from September 28 to 30 to demand a five-day working week. Public-sector lenders such as SBI and PNB warned customers that branch services would be disrupted over quarter-end. None of this explains how Axis Bank's shares have traded.

stocks:ICICIBANK.NS.standing: ICICI Bank is one of India's largest private-sector lenders, based in Mumbai. It lends to both retail customers and companies, so its shares are a closely watched measure of Indian credit demand and the health of the banking system.
stocks:ICICIBANK.NS.recent: The only bank story in the window was a three-day nationwide strike by Indian bank unions demanding a five-day working week, called for September 28 to 30. It falls after the decline and targets public-sector lenders such as SBI and PNB, so it does not explain ICICI Bank's slide.

stocks:HDFCBANK.NS.standing: Shares of HDFC Bank, India's largest private-sector lender, listed on the National Stock Exchange in Mumbai. It carries one of the heaviest weights in India's benchmark indices, so its moves pull the wider market with it.
stocks:HDFCBANK.NS.recent: The only Indian banking news in this period was a three-day nationwide strike by bank unions from September 28 to 30 over a five-day working week. The strike starts after this series ends, and it is centred on public-sector lenders such as SBI and PNB, so it does not explain the move.

stocks:UNH.standing: UnitedHealth Group, the largest US health insurer, owns UnitedHealthcare and the Optum care and pharmacy-benefits business. Its shares move on Medicare Advantage payment rates and on how fast its members' medical costs rise.
stocks:UNH.recent: The only company news came two days after the last close, when UnitedHealthcare dropped prior authorization on 1,700 procedure codes. Nothing reported in the fortnight before explains the slide that came earlier.

poly-will-the-us-announce-a-diesel-expor.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Washington bans diesel exports by October 31. A ban would keep US refiners' output at home, cutting supply to the Latin American and European buyers who import American diesel.

poly-variational-fdv-above-2b-one-day-af.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Variational, a crypto derivatives trading platform, is valued above $2 billion on a fully diluted basis after its token launches. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

poly-bitcoin-all-time-high-by-december-3.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if bitcoin trades above its previous record price at any point before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with bitcoin itself.
poly-bitcoin-all-time-high-by-december-3.recent: The trough came as the Clarity Act's prospects fell apart: Republicans rejected Democrats' counter-proposal on the crypto bill, and Bitcoin slipped with it. None of the reporting since explains the later rebound. New York's suit against Polymarket over illegal gambling is about the venue, not about Bitcoin.

wiki-anthropic.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on Anthropic, the San Francisco company that builds the Claude AI models. It rises when the lab's releases, lawsuits or dealings with governments send people to look up who it is.
wiki-anthropic.recent: 4 paying subscribers sued 4 AI labs, Anthropic among them, over their slowdown deal, and days later the company cut Opus prices 40% with its 5.5 release. A Washington court upheld its blacklisting 2-1, and its IPO prospectus told investors its AI could end humanity. None of it falls on the day of the early-September peak.

wiki-pakistan-tehreek-e-insaf.standing: Pakistan's largest opposition party, founded by former cricketer and prime minister Imran Khan. It governs Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, and its street protests are the main test of the military-backed order in Islamabad.
wiki-pakistan-tehreek-e-insaf.recent: The party spent the fortnight building to a march on Islamabad. Imran Khan's sisters were detained, a provincial minister was seized at gunpoint on a motorway, and the opposition alliance TTAP joined. Chief Minister Sohail Afridi defied Islamabad's threat, talks with the government collapsed, and the march left Lakki Marwat on 4 October.

poly-will-magdalena-andersson-be-the-nex.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Magdalena Andersson, the Social Democrats' leader and a former prime minister, becomes Sweden's next PM. The Riksdag must tolerate the pick, so it trades on coalition arithmetic as much as votes.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-finish-in-seco.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro, a senator and son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, finishes second in the first round of Brazil's presidential election. Second place is the last seat in a run-off.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-finish-in-seco.recent: Brazil votes on Sunday for a president, governors and lawmakers, and the top two go to a run-off if nobody clears half the valid votes. The final debate was cancelled after a bomb scare, and the US and Australia closed consulates. None of that accounts for the shift in what traders will pay for second place.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if shipping through the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal by its deadline. Most Gulf oil and gas exports leave through the strait, so the price is a running bet on that route reopening.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: After three hours of direct talks with Witkoff in New York, Iran offered to reopen Hormuz 7 days after the US agreed, and Trump rejected it. Explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later. Iran said Hormuz authorities will blacklist charterers, and an Iranian missile strike injured eight US Marines, each one a step further from ships moving normally.

poly-will-douard-philippe-win-the-2027-f.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Édouard Philippe, Macron's first prime minister and now mayor of Le Havre, wins France's 2027 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

poly-us-iran-final-nuclear-deal-by-octob.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Washington and Tehran agree a nuclear deal by 31 October 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on that outcome, and it reprices within hours of any signal from either capital.
poly-us-iran-final-nuclear-deal-by-octob.recent: Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, Trump rejected the offer on Saturday, and explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later. Days after that, TASS, citing Axios, reported that Trump would ease sanctions and unfreeze Iran's assets in exchange for nuclear concessions. Mehr said Araghchi was meeting Qatari mediators in New York.

poly-trump-renames-ai-by-september-30.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Donald Trump gives artificial intelligence a new official name before the end of September. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a forecast.
poly-trump-renames-ai-by-september-30.recent: The only AI story of the fortnight that involved Trump himself was his dinner invitation to Anthropic's Dario Amodei for Sunday. None of the reporting, from the dinner or from anything else, has him proposing a new name for AI, so nothing reported explains why traders bid the contract up.

stocks:BP.standing: London-based BP is one of the oil majors, producing, refining and trading oil and gas worldwide; this is its New York-listed share. It moves with crude and with the cash its upstream fields return to shareholders.
stocks:BP.recent: The one BP story in the input arrived after this window closed: Egypt's Petroleum Minister Karim Badawy told BP that Cairo would reject the sale of part of its Egyptian oil and gas assets to Israeli majority-owned Energean, according to sources speaking to Mada Masr. Nothing in the input explains the earlier rise.

stocks:000660.KS.standing: South Korea's second-largest company by market value, listed on the Korea Exchange in Seoul, and one of the world's biggest memory-chip makers. It is a leading supplier of the high-bandwidth memory that AI accelerators depend on.
stocks:000660.KS.recent: SK Hynix was reported to want Intel to make its memory chips in the US, at an Ohio fab, although Intel has not made memory since the 1980s. Together with Samsung it controls 83% of memory chips, and AI hardware depends on that supply. Neither story accounts for the share price's path.

poly-will-marine-le-pen-win-the-2027-fre.standing: What traders on Polymarket pay for a contract that pays out if Marine Le Pen wins France's presidency. Her National Rally wants to curb immigration and the EU's powers in the bloc's second-largest economy.

stocks:7201.T.standing: Shares of Nissan, the Yokohama-based carmaker listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, priced in yen. The stock rides on its sales in the US and China and on its long alliance with France's Renault.
stocks:7201.T.recent: The only story about the company in the fortnight came from Paris: prosecutors asked for a four-year sentence for Rachida Dati over alleged paid lobbying for Renault-Nissan under Carlos Ghosn while she was an MEP. That case covers 2009-2013 and does not explain the fall in the share price.

stocks:MDA.standing: A Canadian space company that builds satellites, antennas and space robotics, the lineage behind the Canadarm arms on the Space Shuttle and the ISS. Its shares move on government and satellite-constellation contracts.
stocks:MDA.recent: The one story touching the company arrived after this chart closes: the ISS's 58-foot Canadarm2, the station's robotic arm, stopped moving after a routine maneuver. Nothing reported before then accounts for the share price.

stocks:NOC.standing: The American defence contractor that builds the B-21 stealth bomber and the Sentinel nuclear missile. Almost all its revenue comes from the US government, so its share moves on the Pentagon budget and programme decisions.
stocks:NOC.recent: Northrop's Talon Blue, its collaborative combat aircraft, completed a first fully autonomous flight at Mojave during the window, a milestone that would ordinarily favour the company. Nothing reported in the fortnight about its own business accounts for the fall in the share.

stocks:MHVYF.standing: Japan's largest defence contractor, quoted here as a US over-the-counter listing in dollars. It builds gas turbines, nuclear plant components and the H3 rocket, so its shares track Tokyo's arms budget and global power demand.

stocks:MRK.standing: Shares in Merck & Co., the New Jersey drugmaker known as MSD outside North America. Its cancer immunotherapy Keytruda is among the world's best-selling drugs, so the stock trades on that franchise and on what replaces it once its patents lapse.
stocks:MRK.recent: The only Merck news of the fortnight came from Rahway at the very end of it: the company quietly stopped supplying a last-resort antibiotic used against drug-resistant infections. It arrived after both the stock's peak and its trough, so it does not account for either.

poly-putin-out-as-president-of-russia-by.standing: What traders on Polymarket will pay for a contract that pays out if Vladimir Putin stops being Russia's president by June 2027. He has held power since 1999, so the price is a running bet on a rupture inside the Kremlin.
poly-putin-out-as-president-of-russia-by.recent: Nothing in the window loosened his hold. Putin's party won Russia's election, Trump invited him to the Miami G20 in December, and the EU removed Russian oligarchs from its sanctions list. Asked about a strikes-only truce with Ukraine, he refused with one word, even as drones set a Moscow oil refinery on fire.

poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-mar.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran hold a diplomatic meeting before the end of September. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it reprices each time either government signals openness or refusal.
poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-mar.recent: Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, and Trump rejected the proposal on Saturday. Explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later, and Tehran said it had seized a second US seabed drone. The only pull the other way was a TASS report, citing Axios, that Trump would offer Iran sanctions relief as Qatar-mediated talks continued.

stocks:MTNOY.standing: Africa's largest mobile operator, based in Johannesburg and listed there; this is its US over-the-counter share. Most of its earnings come from Nigeria, Ghana and South Africa, so swings in the naira and cedi move it.
stocks:MTNOY.recent: The only related report this fortnight, datelined Niamey, found that telecom firms have carried out roughly 100 African internet shutdowns since 2016. Nothing in it explains the share price.

stocks:CRM.standing: Shares of Salesforce, the San Francisco company whose cloud software runs sales, service and marketing for large businesses. It is the bellwether for subscription software, and trades on whether AI agents extend its seat-based model or replace it.
stocks:CRM.recent: The one relevant development was Meta launching a paid AI platform for businesses on Monday, which moved Meta into the enterprise software Salesforce sells. Nothing reported explains the rest of the slide, which began weeks earlier.

stocks:NOW.standing: ServiceNow sells cloud software that large companies use to run IT, HR and customer-service workflows. Its shares are a bellwether for corporate software budgets, and for whether AI adds to seat-based SaaS or replaces it.
stocks:NOW.recent: Meta launched a paid AI platform for businesses, taking a consumer-internet giant straight into the enterprise market where ServiceNow sells its own AI agents. That launch came only at the very end of the window, and nothing else carried here accounts for the slide that preceded it.

stocks:SNOW.standing: Snowflake sells a cloud data platform where companies store and query their corporate data, and bills by usage. Its shares are a gauge of how much enterprises spend on data infrastructure and AI workloads.
stocks:SNOW.recent: The only related news in the fortnight was Meta's launch of a paid AI platform for businesses in Menlo Park, and it came weeks after Snowflake's early-September swings. Nothing in the input explains why the stock moved.

stocks:MDB.standing: Shares of MongoDB, the New York company behind the widely used document database and its Atlas cloud service. Investors treat it as a gauge of how much companies spend on software infrastructure, including building AI applications.
stocks:MDB.recent: Monday's low came the same day Meta launched a paid AI platform for businesses, a move into the enterprise market that software makers sell to. None of the reporting explains the slide over the weeks before that.

poly-will-alexandria-ocasio-cortez-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, the New York congresswoman, wins the 2028 US presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it tracks the Democratic left's standing.
poly-will-alexandria-ocasio-cortez-win-t.recent: None of the fortnight's news touched the 2028 race, so none of it explains the move. The closest story was about the venue itself: New York sued Polymarket for letting 18-to-20-year-olds bet where state law sets 21.

stocks:AXON.standing: Axon Enterprise makes the Taser and the body cameras most US police forces wear, and sells the cloud software that stores their footage. Its revenue rests on multi-year contracts with police departments.
stocks:AXON.recent: The fortnight carried 404 Media asking readers whether their city uses Axon license plate cameras, and a vendor's pitch to Johnson City police to add facial recognition to Flock's plate cameras. Neither accounts for the fall in the share price.

poly-will-anthropic-ipo-by-december-31-2.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI models, lists its shares on a public exchange before the deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in cents on the dollar.

stocks:AMD.standing: The Santa Clara chipmaker that is Nvidia's main rival in AI accelerators and Intel's in PC and server processors. Its share price is a running bet on whether anyone can win AI data-centre spending away from Nvidia.
stocks:AMD.recent: The one big AMD story of the fortnight came after the rally, not before it: AMD agreed to pay $8.2 billion for Fei-Fei Li's World Labs, a 'world model' startup. The bet is that owning the software layer is how a chipmaker loosens Nvidia's CUDA-driven lock on AI compute. None of the reporting accounts for the climb before the deal.

poly-us-iran-final-nuclear-deal-by-decem.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US and Iran sign a final nuclear agreement by the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on talks, sanctions and fighting in the Gulf.
poly-us-iran-final-nuclear-deal-by-decem.recent: Talks in New York turned on the terms for reopening Hormuz. Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen the strait within 7 days. Hours later, explosions hit Qeshm Island, and Iran said it had seized a second US seabed drone. Two days after that, TASS, citing Axios, reported that Trump would offer Iran sanctions relief.

poly-will-samuel-alito-announce-his-reti.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Justice Samuel Alito announces his retirement from the US Supreme Court before 2026 ends. He is one of the court's oldest conservatives, and when he leaves decides which president and Senate fill the seat.

poly-iran-charges-hormuz-fees-by-septemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Iran imposes transit fees on ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz by its deadline. About a fifth of the world's seaborne oil passes through the strait, so a toll there reaches every tanker.
poly-iran-charges-hormuz-fees-by-septemb.recent: Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, and Trump rejected the offer. Explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later. Mehr then said Hormuz authorities would blacklist charterers, which threatens the ships themselves rather than charging them a fee. Meanwhile the New York talks centred on the terms for reopening, and Trump weighed sanctions relief.

poly-another-fed-rate-hike-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US Federal Reserve raises its policy rate at least once more before 2026 ends. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on inflation data and on what Fed officials say.
poly-another-fed-rate-hike-in-2026.recent: The Fed voted 12-0 to raise rates because a closed strait had pushed up prices, defied Trump's calls to lower rates, and signalled more to come. That turned the bet into a question of whether it would move again this year. A week later, traders were pricing in 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-kansas.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Republican candidate wins Kansas's US Senate seat in November 2026. Kansas has not sent a Democrat to the Senate since the 1930s, so the price is a bet on whether that record holds.

wiki-france.standing: How many times the Wikipedia article on France is opened each day. It jumps when an election, a strike or an attack sends readers abroad looking for the country behind the story.
wiki-france.recent: National Rally won at least 14 Senate seats on Sunday, enough for its first group in the chamber, the same weekend Pope Leo pressed France on clerical abuse at Lourdes. High school protests then spread: 164 arrests, a public-sector strike unions put at 300,000, and pupils disrupting 564 schools on Friday.

poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US and Iran hold another meeting before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on every sign that talks are opening or breaking down.
poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-dec.recent: Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, and explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later. The next day TASS, citing Axios, said Trump would offer Iran sanctions relief. Then Mehr News Agency reported that the US had answered Tehran's Hormuz conditions, so the channel had reopened after the rejection.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the ceasefire between Israel and Iran survives to the end of October. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on strikes, talks and any incident either side blames on the other.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The US answered Iran's 7-day proposal through Qatar, keeping a channel open. Pulling the other way, Trump vowed a tough response if Iran is linked to the flydubai cockpit incident on a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, and Iran's foreign ministry confirmed serious debate on quitting the nuclear treaty. None of it accounts for the earlier climb.

stocks:PBR.standing: Brazil's state-controlled oil company, traded in New York as dollar shares. Its deep-water output off Brazil ties it to crude, and Brasília's say over fuel prices and dividends ties it to politics.
stocks:PBR.recent: The only Petrobras news in the fortnight was a test of the Cardano blockchain to verify low-carbon fuel claims, and nothing in it accounts for the share price.

stocks:UBSFY.standing: Ubisoft, the French publisher behind Assassin's Creed and Far Cry, quoted here as a dollar share traded over the counter in the US. Its fortunes rest on a handful of big-budget releases a year.
stocks:UBSFY.recent: The one development touching the industry was an EU consumer investigation, run from Brussels, into how 9 video game companies sell virtual currencies. It came after this window closed, and nothing in it accounts for the share price.

stocks:EADSY.standing: Airbus's US over-the-counter shares, priced in dollars. Airbus builds roughly half the world's large passenger jets, so the stock turns on delivery rates, engine and supplier bottlenecks, and the euro.
stocks:EADSY.recent: The fortnight's only Airbus news was ESA picking Airbus Defence and Space and OHB to lead parallel feasibility studies for a European-led low-Earth-orbit station. That is a study contract in the space unit, and it does not account for the slide in a company whose value rests on airliners.

poly-will-samuel-alito-announce-his-reti.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Samuel Alito, a conservative US Supreme Court justice since 2006, announces his retirement by June 2027. A departure hands the president a nomination and the Senate a confirmation fight.

poly-will-anthropic-have-the-best-ai-mod.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic's model ranks first among AI models at the month's end. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves when a rival lab ships a new model.

poly-will-google-have-the-best-ai-model-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Google's model ranks as the best AI model at the year-end deadline, judged by a public leaderboard. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each lab's model releases.
poly-will-google-have-the-best-ai-model-.recent: The fortnight's news about this venue was legal, not technical: New York sued Polymarket for taking bets from 18-to-20-year-olds where state law sets 21, and an appeals court let states regulate Kalshi's sports contracts. None of it concerns Google's models or accounts for the repricing.

poly-iran-leadership-change-by-october-3.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Iran's top leadership changes before a fixed deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on the Islamic Republic's highest office changing hands, whether by death, removal or collapse.
poly-iran-leadership-change-by-october-3.recent: Traders paid less for a change at the top as Washington kept dealing with the government in Tehran. Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz and explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later, yet Mehr says the US then answered Iran's conditions, and TASS, citing Axios, said Trump would offer sanctions relief.

poly-will-sorin-grindeanu-be-the-next-pr.standing: A contract that pays if Sorin Grindeanu, a Social Democrat who has held the office before, becomes Romania's next prime minister. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves on coalition politics in Bucharest.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-us-pr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Marco Rubio, the Florida Republican, wins the 2028 US presidential election. Its price is what bettors will pay for that outcome, and it moves with his standing in the Republican field.
poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-us-pr.recent: The fortnight's news about the market itself was legal, not political: New York sued Polymarket for letting 18-to-20-year-olds bet where state law sets 21. None of it concerned Rubio or the 2028 race, and none of it accounts for the price.

stocks:C.standing: Shares of Citigroup, one of Wall Street's largest banks, listed on the New York Stock Exchange. More of its revenue comes from outside the US than any big American lender's, so the stock follows global trade and dollar funding flows.

poly-gemini-4pt0-released-by-october-31-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Google publicly releases a model named Gemini 4.0 by the stated deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on leaks, launch events and rival releases.

poly-trump-out-as-president-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Donald Trump stops being US president before 2027, whether by death, resignation or removal. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on health, legal and political shocks.
poly-trump-out-as-president-before-2027.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news pointed to an early exit: Trump hosted Xi in Washington, rejected Iran's Hormuz proposal, unveiled an Iowa steel mill before the midterms and won a Supreme Court order reviving third-country deportations. With no such event, the bet loses value as the deadline nears and fewer days remain for it to pay.

poly-will-flavio-bolsonaro-win-the-most-.standing: The price traders pay on Polymarket for Flávio Bolsonaro, senator and eldest son of Jair Bolsonaro, finishing first in the opening round of Brazil's presidential election. A runoff follows if no candidate clears half the vote.

wiki-diesel-fuel.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on diesel, the fuel that trucks, ships, trains, farm machinery and backup generators burn. Its price feeds into the cost of nearly everything that is transported.
wiki-diesel-fuel.recent: Trump told Europe to release its diesel reserves or lose US supply, after weeks of weighing a 90-day export ban to bring down a record price at home. France proposed a joint release, and the International Energy Agency said it will release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel. US diesel is up 70% since the Iran war began.

stocks:POWERGRID.NS.standing: India's state-owned transmission utility, which owns and runs most of the high-voltage lines carrying power between states. Its earnings are regulated returns on the lines it builds, so the stock follows government grid spending.
stocks:POWERGRID.NS.recent: New Delhi approved ₹1.86 lakh crore for transmission lines, a scheme for 135 GW of renewables, on the last day of the window. That is money for the business this company is in, and it arrived after the slide rather than before it; nothing else from the fortnight accounts for the fall.

stocks:NTPC.NS.standing: India's largest electricity producer, majority-owned by the government and listed on the National Stock Exchange. Most of its output is coal-fired, so its shares track the country's power demand and fuel policy.
stocks:NTPC.NS.recent: New Delhi approved ₹1.86 lakh crore for transmission lines, money that goes to the grid that carries power rather than to the plants that generate it. Nothing else in the fortnight's news touches the company, and that approval does not account for the share price.

poly-iran-charges-hormuz-fees-by-october.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Iran starts charging ships a fee to transit the Strait of Hormuz before its deadline. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through the strait, so a toll there reaches every importer.
poly-iran-charges-hormuz-fees-by-october.recent: The fee stayed a bargaining position rather than a charge. Talks in New York focused on Hormuz reopening terms; Trump rejected Iran's Hormuz proposal, and Mehr News Agency says the US has since answered Tehran's conditions. Hormuz authorities threatened to blacklist charterers, and an Iranian missile strike injured eight US Marines.

stocks:BYD.standing: A Las Vegas-based casino operator listed on the New York Stock Exchange, running regional and locals-market casinos across several US states. Its shares move with American consumer spending on leisure and gambling.

stocks:PL.standing: Shares in a San Francisco company that runs hundreds of small Earth-imaging satellites and photographs most of the planet's land every day. Governments, defence agencies, farmers and newsrooms buy the pictures.

stocks:LCID.standing: An American maker of luxury electric cars, majority-owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. It spends far more than it earns from sales, so the share price tracks how long Riyadh keeps funding it.
stocks:LCID.recent: The Saudi fund that owns Lucid is also behind a new rival electric-car maker in Riyadh, which leaves the company competing with its own shareholder's other venture. That story surfaced after the shares had already fallen and does not account for the slide.

stocks:SHEL.standing: The New York-listed shares of a London-based oil and gas major, one of the world's largest traders of liquefied natural gas. They move with crude and gas prices, and British pension funds lean on the dividend.
stocks:SHEL.recent: Advocacy outlet Declassified UK reported that Shell and BP have signed Venezuelan agreements since January, and Nigeria's attorney-general said one oil treaty dispute exposed the country to over $2 billion, a threat to cleanup after oil divestment. Neither accounts for the share price.

stocks:MU.standing: A US maker of DRAM and NAND memory chips, based in Boise, Idaho, and one of three firms that produce nearly all the world's DRAM. Its shares follow memory prices, which swing harder than the rest of the chip industry.
stocks:MU.recent: Micron says demand for memory will exceed supply for at least 2 years, a shortage that leaves chipmakers setting the price rather than buyers. The statement from Boise came after the climb, so it describes the conditions behind the move rather than the trigger for any single day.

stocks:CHGG.standing: A US online education company that sells homework help and study subscriptions to students. Its business depends on students finding it through search, which makes it one of the stocks most exposed to AI chatbots answering the question first.
stocks:CHGG.recent: A judge in Washington dismissed the antitrust suits that Chegg and Penske had brought against Google over its AI Overviews, ending the company's attempt to challenge them in court. The ruling came at the very end of the window, so it does not account for the slide that preceded it.

poly-will-anthropic-have-the-highest-ipo.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, maker of the Claude AI models, is the largest stock-market debut of 2026 by market value. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a forecast.

wiki-united-kingdom.standing: How many times a day people open the English Wikipedia article on the United Kingdom. It counts readers, not events: the line jumps when something sends a global audience looking for the country's basics.
wiki-united-kingdom.recent: A suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford, the base used by the US for the Iran war, brought a seventh arrest, a British-Iranian man among those held, and the US withdrew all 12 B-1 bombers. Iran denies any link. Two Iranians were charged over a Yom Kippur plot in Manchester. None of this accounts for the earlier peak, which came before these events.

poly-will-renan-santos-finish-in-third-p.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Renan Santos, a founder of the Free Brazil Movement, finishes third in the first round of Brazil's presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

poly-will-the-republican-party-control-t.standing: What traders on Polymarket pay for a contract that pays out if Republicans hold the US Senate after the midterm elections. The Senate confirms judges and cabinet officers, so control decides whom a president can appoint.

stocks:NST.AX.standing: One of Australia's largest gold miners, listed in Sydney and run from Perth, with mines around Kalgoorlie in Western Australia and in Alaska. Its shares are a geared bet on the gold price: costs are largely fixed, so profit swings harder than the metal.
stocks:NST.AX.recent: South Africa's Gold Fields offered A$39bn for the company, and the board in Perth turned it down. A takeover approach puts an outside buyer's valuation on the shares, and this one came from a foreign miner seeking to consolidate Australia's gold producers, so the stock traded on the bid, not on the metal alone.

stocks:GFI.standing: A Johannesburg-based gold miner with mines in South Africa, Ghana, Australia, Peru and Chile; these are its New York-listed shares. Its costs are largely fixed, so its profit and its share price swing harder than the gold price.
stocks:GFI.recent: Gold Fields offered A$39bn for Northern Star, the Perth gold miner, and was turned down. A bid that size is paid for by the buyer's own shareholders, and an acquirer's stock is usually sold when one lands. Nothing here dates the approach, so its link to the slide is unproven.

poly-will-sudans-emergency-response-room.standing: What traders will pay for a contract that pays out if the Nobel Peace Prize goes to Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms, the volunteer networks running kitchens and clinics through the civil war. The Norwegian committee decides in secret.

stocks:AAL.standing: The share price of American Airlines, the largest US carrier by passengers flown, listed on Nasdaq. Jet fuel and labour are its biggest costs and it carries heavy debt, so the stock moves on oil prices and on demand for travel.

stocks:LMT.standing: The largest US defence contractor and maker of the F-35 and F-16 fighter jets. Most of its revenue comes from the US government, and every foreign sale needs Washington's approval, so its shares follow defence budgets and arms deals.
stocks:LMT.recent: The peak came as the Trump administration approved the sale of F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia, opening a new customer for Lockheed's biggest programme. Nothing since explains the slide: the first 2 of 66 F-16V fighters Taiwan ordered landed in Taipei on Friday, a delivery against an existing order rather than new business.

stocks:TECK.standing: A Vancouver-based miner whose shares trade in New York and Toronto. Its earnings come mostly from copper and zinc, from mines in Canada, Chile and Peru, so the stock moves with the copper price and with output at those sites.
stocks:TECK.recent: China's antitrust regulator asked Anglo American to commit to a steady supply of copper concentrate as a condition for approving its $54bn merger with Teck, sources told Reuters. Beijing holds that lever because its smelters buy most of the world's concentrate. The demand came after the swings shown here and does not explain them.

poly-will-the-international-court-of-jus.standing: A contract that pays out if the International Court of Justice, the UN's top court in The Hague, is awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, set by their bets.

poly-will-lula-win-the-most-votes-in-the.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins the first round of Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Brazil goes to a runoff if no candidate clears half the valid votes.
poly-will-lula-win-the-most-votes-in-the.recent: Two days before Sunday's vote, polls put Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a dead heat. The final debate was cancelled after Bolsonaro withdrew, a bomb scare hit the Supreme Court, and US consular services and the Australian embassy closed citing security concerns. None of it dates to the September slide in the betting.

poly-will-indiana-enact-a-data-center-mo.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Indiana enacts a statewide pause on new data centers before 2027. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, in a state where server farms compete with households for power and water.

poly-will-anthropic-announce-bankruptcy-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the AI lab behind Claude, files for bankruptcy by the end of 2027. The price is what traders pay for that outcome: a bet on whether AI revenue outruns the cost of compute.

poly-will-oklahoma-enact-a-data-center-m.standing: A contract that pays out if Oklahoma passes a law pausing new data center construction before 2027. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it turns on a state weighing power and water demand against investment.

poly-will-texas-enact-a-data-center-mora.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Texas passes a law halting new data center construction by its deadline. Texas is among the largest US sites for the AI build-out, and its isolated grid has to power it.

stocks:VIC.VN.standing: Vietnam's largest private conglomerate, listed in Ho Chi Minh City, spanning property developer Vinhomes and carmaker VinFast. It is among the heaviest weights in the VN-Index, so its share price pulls the whole market.
stocks:VIC.VN.recent: The news from Hanoi in this stretch was about power rather than this company: LNG supplies just 1.6% of Vietnam's electricity, a shortfall that stands in the way of the country's chip plan. None of it accounts for the share price.

poly-will-ohio-enact-a-data-center-morat.standing: A contract that pays out if Ohio halts new data center construction before its deadline. Central Ohio is one of the largest US clusters of server farms, and their power demand feeds into electricity bills across the state.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: Nvidia authorized a record $150 billion share buyback in late September, its biggest ever, which retires stock and raises each remaining share's claim on profit. Days later Trump hosted its chief executive as top tech firms signed an accord to self-police AI development.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: A federal jury in San Diego awarded Taction Technology $5.72 billion from Apple in a haptics patent case, in the same week the company pulled its strongest iCloud encryption from new UK users. Apple Pay then launched in India on Axis Bank cards only, outside the UPI system that market runs on. None of it explains the share's rise.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: The share rose in late September on Google's Suncatcher plan, an orbital data center test satellite built around its TPUs. Since then a judge dismissed the Chegg and Penske antitrust suits, and Gemini 4 Argon arrived after months of delays, released only to trusted cyber defenders. None of it accounts for the slide since August.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: The past fortnight brought a new line of Kindles and accessories ahead of Prime Big Deal Days, and a YouTube Shopping partnership with Amazon in India. Neither accounts for the swing in the share over the summer.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: Microsoft committed more than $10 billion across 4 Gulf states by 2030, selling cloud and AI capacity as resilience. In the same week it cut 268 Xbox jobs and handed Halo to Activision, and contractors were found to be reviewing images Copilot users upload. None of that accounts for the climb in the share.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: Starship reached orbit for the first time on Flight 14, and did so after losing 1 of its 3 main Raptor engines, a failure that bears on NASA's moon mission. Days later NASA and SpaceX launched Crew-13 to the International Space Station. Iran, meanwhile, says it stopped Starlink operating in the war.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: The run-up centred on Meta Connect, where the company showed its Muse AI agent and camera-free Ray-Ban glasses at $349, and Wall Street took Muse as its next catalyst. Since then a Santa Fe jury found Meta deceived consumers 44 million times, and the company rushed fixes for a Muse flaw that opened a path to its internal databases.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: An 11-day pipeline shutdown stopped the company's Red Sea crude loadings at Yanbu until late September. The Houthis then said they struck an oil facility near Riyadh, with smoke seen near Aramco, and 2 tankers were hit in Hormuz. Its CEO said almost 3 billion barrels of supply were lost and replenishing stocks could take two years.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla's sales fell 2 percent in the third quarter, a result reported as underwhelming. In Fremont, workers balked at training the Optimus humanoid robots meant to replace them, and the company reportedly stopped Model S and X production in May. None of that explains the share's swings.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Samsung and SK Hynix together control 83% of memory chips, a concentration that has made Korea a chokepoint for the memory that AI systems depend on. Nothing reported in the period accounts for the share's move.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: Micron said memory demand will exceed supply for at least 2 years, and its chief executive described supplies as only getting tighter. The pull comes from AI demand, and a shortage that long leaves the chipmaker, not its customers, setting the price of what it sells.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.
co:amd.recent: AMD agreed on Sep 28 to pay $8.2 billion for World Labs, the world models startup of AI pioneer Fei-Fei Li. The purchase came late in the share's climb, and nothing else reported about the company's own business in that stretch accounts for the rest of it.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.
co:jpmorgan.recent: Fed officials questioned JPMorgan, along with Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley, in a review prompted by worries about private credit, the lending that banks finance through funds outside the banking system. The questioning came at the very end of the window and does not account for the share's earlier slide.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: Samsung and SK Hynix together control 83% of memory chips, a concentration that makes the two Seoul companies a chokepoint for AI hardware. Nothing reported in the window accounts for the fall in the share.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
co:asml.recent: BofA said a chip technology move by ASML threatens the shares of Besi. That note is about what the move does to Besi, and nothing else in the fortnight's news explains ASML's own share.

us-2y.standing: The interest the US government pays to borrow for two years. It follows where traders think the Federal Reserve will set rates more closely than any other maturity, and short-term loan rates worldwide move with it.
us-2y.recent: The fortnight's news carries the question rather than the answer: what Washington does next if US bond yields keep rising. Nothing in it names the cause of the climb.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, surveyed weekly by Freddie Mac. It follows long-dated Treasury yields and sets the monthly cost of buying a house for most American borrowers.

ez-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in consumer prices across the countries that use the euro, as measured by Eurostat. The European Central Bank sets interest rates to hold it at 2%, so borrowing costs for the whole bloc follow it.
ez-cpi.recent: The September figure, published after this line ends, came in at 3.8%, the highest level in three years. That keeps pressure on the ECB to hike rates. The reports of the jump name no cause for it.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva finishes first in Brazil's presidential first round with a lead of 5 to 10 percentage points over the runner-up. Its price is what traders are betting, not a poll.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.recent: Brazil votes on Sunday for a president, governors and lawmakers, and a candidate needs more than half the valid votes to avoid a run-off. Nothing reported in the past fortnight accounts for the change in what traders will pay for this margin.

bnb.standing: The token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders spend it on transaction fees there and on trading discounts at Binance, so its price follows the fortunes of the world's largest crypto exchange.

trx.standing: The native token of the Tron blockchain, used to pay for transactions and to stake for the network's resources. Tron carries a large share of the world's Tether transfers, so its token's price tracks demand for moving dollar stablecoins.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, a network built for fast, cheap transactions. Fees and staking are paid in it, so its price follows how much trading, stablecoin and app activity the chain carries.
sol.recent: Alpenglow, the network's settlement upgrade, reached its second public test network in late September. It targets 150-millisecond finality, down from 12.8 seconds, which puts the chain within reach of trading desks. The Solana Foundation followed by launching DvP to settle institutional trades in seconds.

xrp.standing: The token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built to move money between banks and across borders. Ripple, the company behind it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: The XRP Ledger retried an upgrade letting banks split payment and compliance duties, then validators reset its activation clock, delaying it 10 days, over a bug that could drain balances. Days later a hacker who took $350 million from the exchange Bitget moved $83 million of it as XRP, which Ripple cannot freeze.

hype.standing: HYPE is the token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders take leveraged positions without a broker. A share of the exchange's trading fees goes to buying the token back, tying its price to trading volume.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched in 2013 as a joke about a dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has no cash flows behind it, so its price is a gauge of retail speculative appetite and moves on social-media attention.
doge.recent: The one development in the window was technical: Dogecoin got an Ethereum-style testnet for trading, lending and stablecoins, a trial of the kind of applications the coin has not hosted before. Nothing in it accounts for the price.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design that lets users hide the sender, receiver and amount of a payment using zero-knowledge proofs. It trades as a bet on whether private digital cash can coexist with regulators and exchanges.
zec.recent: The late-September climb came as two things landed together: researchers proposed Zcash-style private payments for Bitcoin without a fork, and developers moved Udon, part of the Tachyon scaling code, into the network's shared cryptography library. Gemini then switched its Zcash software ahead of 25-second blocks, which reached public testnet early.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of independent operators that feeds outside data such as asset prices into blockchain smart contracts. Many decentralised lending apps rely on its price feeds, and LINK pays for them.
link.recent: The peak came the day after Chainlink launched CCIP 2.0, a new version of the protocol that gives big crypto apps more control over their security. Nothing else in the period's news accounts for the earlier slide or the pullback since.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: For a decade the Bank of Japan held rates near zero on the argument that underlying inflation was still short of its 2% target. Three sources told Reuters the bank is weighing saying this month that the target is roughly met, which removes its own stated reason to hold. Oil prices since the war on Iran have raised Japanese import costs.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark Chinese banks use to price most new business and household loans, published monthly under the People's Bank of China. It sets what credit costs in the world's second-largest economy.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia's published business in the past fortnight was routine: it set the official dollar rate at 83.25 rubles for October 2 and reported no yuan purchases or sales. Neither accounts for the cuts.

stocks:NSRGY.standing: The world's largest food company, based in Vevey, Switzerland, selling Nescafé, KitKat, Maggi and infant formula in nearly every country. Its sales track what households pay for groceries, and what cocoa and coffee cost.
stocks:NSRGY.recent: India's food regulator, the FSSAI, failed a sample of Nestlé dairy whitener as unsafe and substandard; Nestlé says the product is safe. The finding arrived after the last trading day shown here, so it accounts for none of the slide on the chart.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-first-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro finishes first in the opening round of Brazil's presidential election with a margin under five points. Its price is what traders will pay for a narrow lead, not a forecast.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-first-.recent: Brazil voted on Sunday for a president, governors and lawmakers, and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro took an early lead over President Lula as the first returns came in. Traders bought a narrow first-place finish rather than an outright win: a candidate needs more than half the valid votes, or the top two go to a run-off.

stocks:SPCX.standing: Elon Musk's rocket and satellite company. It carries most of the world's payload to orbit, flies NASA's astronauts and runs the Starlink internet constellation, so its fortunes rest on launch cadence and state contracts.
stocks:SPCX.recent: Starship reached orbit for the first time on Flight 14, despite losing one of its three main Raptor engines, a failure that raised questions for NASA's moon mission. Within days Elon Musk was named co-lead of a Pentagon study of future warfare and the company launched Crew-13 to the International Space Station.

poly-will-augusto-cury-finish-in-third-p.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the candidate Cury finishes third in the first round of Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Third place is watched because that candidate's voters are the ones the two run-off contenders must win.
poly-will-augusto-cury-finish-in-third-p.recent: The contract repriced as the count arrived. Brazil voted on Sunday for a president, governors and lawmakers, and early returns put Senator Flavio Bolsonaro ahead of President Lula, with the top two going to a run-off unless one clears half the valid votes. The published tallies name only those two, so the order behind them is what traders settled as results came in.

poly-israel-accuses-iranproxies-of-plane.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Israel formally blames Iran for a stabbing aboard a passenger aircraft before its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a forecast of it.
poly-israel-accuses-iranproxies-of-plane.recent: The bet follows a cockpit altercation on flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The UAE opened a terrorism probe and Trump vowed a tough response if Iran was linked, but Israel's own agencies then turned on each other over the co-pilot's vetting, while the US answered Iran's 7-day plan through Qatar.
